D-015high riskdocs/decisions/wi-798.toml

Decided

Review 005's MAJOR (OpenCode) is answered by construction, not a list: OpenCode loads a provider from the first set variable of any catalog provider's env names (226 providers on this box, a catalog fetched and refreshed hourly), honours each provider SDK's own default key even with the provider's env list emptied, and takes OPENCODE_AUTH_CONTENT in place of the home's auth.json (the builder read the installed opencode-ai 1.18.30's embedded source and reproduced the leak against a local listener). A hand list cannot be sourced and drifts. So a qualified OpenCode launch composes its environment from a declared base (platform variables: path, system and user directories, temp, terminal, locale, and the network-transport variables a proxy or CA bundle needs, none of them a credential) plus the route's and account's declared pairs and the account home, never from the ambient environment; a variable the base leaves out is declared on the route or account. An unqualified OpenCode entry keeps today's environment exactly. claude, codex and gemini keep their sourced withheld lists (D-008, D-009); moving them to the same base is not built here.

Alternative passed over

(B) confine to the route's declared provider through enabled_providers, which still admits that provider's ambient key; (C) a name pattern such as *_API_KEY, which cannot be sourced and both over- and under-withholds.

Reversal cost

Low to medium: one composition rule for one CLI, plus its tests.

Why not escalated

It is the spec's Trust rule (a declared account's own credentials, no ambient fallback) at the boundary that already owns it; the only construction that ends the class for an open-ended credential set. High risk because a qualified OpenCode launch that relied on an undeclared ambient variable now fails until the route or account declares it.

D-004high riskdocs/decisions/wi-806.toml

Decided

The landing's squash is exempt at the hook by verification, not by trust. While git's own SQUASH_MSG names a squashed tip, the exemption holds only when HEAD is an ancestor of that tip (the lane was rebased onto trunk, as acts serialize and integrate's own trunk_is_ancestor already requires) AND the index's approval-act registries and record are byte-equal to the tip's own; then each commit HEAD..tip is judged against its parents, as the slot does, and the index is not. Otherwise the index is judged like any commit, and a refusal ends with a hint to rebase the lane onto trunk first. check.py reads SQUASH_MSG; acceptance_record takes the tip. Amended twice after Sol REVIEW-A: r1 (MAJOR) found the first build's intersection of the index's changes against HEAD and the tip let a SQUASH_MSG left by an abandoned squash exempt a different direct commit; r2 (BLOCKER) found the round-1 rule (equality to git merge-tree --write-tree of the tip into HEAD) admitted a squash that git combined, from a trunk and a lane each editing a different line of one multiline cell, into a THIRD cell value no judged commit carried. The merge-tree dependency (git 2.38+) is dropped, not kept beside this rule.

Alternative passed over

(a) No hook exemption, so a hand landing of an act-taking lane needs --no-verify; (b) exempt any commit while SQUASH_MSG exists; (c) also refuse a hand-typed commit whose spine and record are byte-identical to the lane tip's; (d) round 1's rule, equality to git's merge of the tip into HEAD, which needs git 2.38 and admits a combined third value; (e) require the landing to introduce no cell value beyond the two judged trees, a per-cell three-way comparison.

Reversal cost

Drop the squashed argument, _squash_lines, SQUASH_REBASE_HINT and the SQUASH_MSG read: about twenty lines and four tests.

Why not escalated

Q-8 exempts the landing squash because the guard held on every lane commit, and a coordinator's hand landing never meets the merge slot, so only re-judging those commits makes that premise true there. Requiring a tip that contains HEAD makes the premise exact rather than approximate: the squash of a refreshed lane is its tip's tree for these files, so every staged spine and record byte is a judged commit's, a combined value included (the refresh carries it as its own judged commit). (e) would rebuild a merge check beside git's; a lane must be rebased before its act anyway, so it adds nothing. RESIDUE, left deliberately and narrowed: after an abandoned squash whose tip contains HEAD, a direct commit whose approval-act registries and record are byte-identical to that TIP's own is still exempt. Every byte of it was committed and judged in the lane, and the window is one commit: git deletes SQUASH_MSG at the next commit, and once trunk moves the tip no longer contains HEAD. Nothing at commit time tells it apart from the squash itself (git keeps no other squash state); option (c) would need a provenance record, which the owner's 'enforce at the commit, no marker convention' rule rules out. Any other spine text or record content beside it is judged plainly. High-risk for the owner's look because it keys hook behaviour on SQUASH_MSG; the residue is Sol's retained MAJOR, for the adjudicator.

D-001high riskdocs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

The overrule coupling runs inside the existing ruling sync: acceptance_record.ruling_sync_lines now returns the open-item lines plus overrule_sync_lines over the same diff, so the pre-commit hook's ruling-sync step and the merge slot's _ruling_sync_refusal judge it with no new step, rung or flag. check.py and integrate.py change in docstrings only.

Alternative passed over

A separate overrule-sync step in check.py's step list and a separate merge-slot rung in integrate.py, each calling its own staged/commit pair.

Reversal cost

Low: split overrule_sync_lines out of ruling_sync_lines and add a step and a rung; the tests call the same public functions and would move with them. Adopters would add the new step to their hook's --run-steps list.

Why not escalated

The build prompt says to reuse the OI-102 Q3 commit-vs-parent shape and not invent a second mechanism; one function over two trees in both places is that shape. Folding also keeps the WI-806 and WI-822 landing conflicts in check.py and integrate.py to docstring lines.

D-004high riskdocs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

The citing work item must be a spec under docs/work/queued/ or docs/work/active/ that the SAME commit adds or changes, whose new text carries the token docs/decisions/<run>.toml#D-NNN (a digit never following the id). A row that already cited the entry and is left untouched, and an archived (terminal) row, do not satisfy the overrule.

Alternative passed over

Accept any open row whose spec cites the entry in the new tree, touched or not; or accept a citation from any spec, archived included.

Reversal cost

Low: widen the filter in overrule_sync_lines (read every open spec of the new tree instead of the diff's) and flip two test cases.

Why not escalated

The spec's words are 'files or amends' in 'the same commit', which names the act, not a standing citation; an untouched earlier citation would let an overrule land with nothing changed to the new direction. The citation form was the build's to fix.

D-005high riskdocs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

The overrule sync fails CLOSED: a commit whose tree carries a decisions record (one the diff touches) that does not parse as TOML is refused, at the pre-commit ruling-sync step and per lane commit at the merge slot, naming the record and the parse error. A parent side that does not parse reads as overruling nothing, so the commit that repairs it owes the citing work for every overrule the repaired record shows.

Alternative passed over

Read an unparseable record as overruling nothing on either side (the round-1 build), so an overrule hidden behind a syntax error is owed by the commit that makes it readable; or refuse an unparseable parent side too, as the open-item ruling sync does.

Reversal cost

Low: newly_overruled raises on an unparseable after-side and _owed_overrules turns that into a refusal line; reversing is the two branches. A lane already carrying such a commit needs its history rewritten to land.

Why not escalated

The round-1 fail-open reading let an overrule plus a syntax error pass both admission points, and a later repair that dropped the verdict passed too (Sol, round-1 MAJOR 1); the owner's standing rule forbids degenerate paths. Refusing only the new side, not the parent, mirrors the open-item sync's unreadable-is-not-unchanged rule without stranding the repair of a record broken before this rule: the repair is judged as overruling everything it shows, which is the strict reading.

D-013high riskdocs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

The citation delimiter '#' joins the run-name alphabet's excluded set, and record_path REFUSES it: a run name carrying '#' raises ValueError naming the run and the character, and the merge slot's decisions-record rung reads that as an absent record, refused when one is owed. The citation pattern's path class cannot contain '#', so the first '#' after docs/decisions/ ends the path, and since no record name carries '#' that one parse is also the right one. A branch named owner.toml#D-002 or owner#cleanup has no record, and the token docs/decisions/owner.toml#D-002 only ever cites owner.toml's D-002. (Corrected in round 5, dispute 1 ruling: round 4 mapped '#' to '-', so owner#cleanup silently wrote, and could be satisfied by, owner-cleanup's record.)

Alternative passed over

Map '#' to '-' (the round-4 build, rejected by the dispute 1 ruling: a lossy rewrite of a git-valid character folds two branch names into one record); escape run names injectively, which moves every slash-named record; or keep '#' in run names and anchor the citation reader to the last .toml#D-<digits> in a token.

Reversal cost

Low: record_path's refusal and the rung's ValueError arm. A branch carrying '#' must be renamed before its lane can merge under a recording dial, and an adopter's record already named with '#' cannot be cited until it is renamed. The alphabet test pins the set against git.

Why not escalated

Sol round 3 MAJOR 1 asks that the producer and the reader leave one parse, and the dispute 1 ruling (Sol round 4 MAJOR upheld) settles the shape: refuse '#' rather than map it, which fails closed, adds no degenerate path and moves no record of any adopter (every name without '#' keeps trunk's path). The refusal reaches only a branch a person named by hand, under a recording dial, at the merge slot: no lane name in this kit produces '#' (lanes are wi-<stem>, session tags are sanitized). It stays high-risk for the owner, as the ruling directs. The residue is stated, not fixed here: a/b and a-b, and a reused branch name, still share one record (the ruling's finding F1, the owner's call).

D-014high riskdocs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

A path list is decoded losslessly, and a path that is not UTF-8 is refused where it would be read. git_paths reads git's bytes and decodes UTF-8 with surrogateescape, so a byte that is not UTF-8 survives as a lone surrogate and the path round-trips to git's exact bytes. git_show, the one blob reader, raises UnreadableBlob for such a path before asking git, naming it with the byte written as a hex escape, and ruling_sync_lines' existing handler makes that a refusal line (its message reworded to name both causes). So a decisions record in the diff, an open spec read when an overrule is owed, and a citing row or the registry in the open-item arm are refused when their path is not UTF-8, while a non-UTF-8 path the syncs never read (a source file, say) is listed and left alone.

Alternative passed over

Decode strictly in git_paths and refuse, by an exception or by answering None, whenever any listed path is not UTF-8 (the build prompt's sketch).

Reversal cost

Low: git_paths' decode and the guard at the head of git_show. Two tests pin the boundary: a non-UTF-8 record refused at the commit and the merge slot, and a non-UTF-8 unrelated path not refused.

Why not escalated

Both shapes fail closed on Sol's probe. A strict listing would refuse every commit touching any non-UTF-8 path anywhere in a repository (a path git accepts), at the pre-commit hook and the merge slot, for a rule that only reads decisions records and work-item specs; the lossless listing refuses exactly the paths the syncs read, at the one blob reader they all share. The guard precedes the git call because a lone surrogate on a Windows command line reaches git as another path, which git answers as absent: the original defect. Known edge: a commit deleting or renaming a non-UTF-8 decisions record is refused too, since its parent side cannot be read; this rule refuses the commit that adds such a record, so one can only predate it, and reading it would need a second, stdin-fed blob reader. The shape also keeps acceptance_record.py at 998 SLOC, where a new exception and handler would pass the 1000 threshold.

D-001high riskdocs/decisions/wi-821.toml

Decided

docs/stack.ini [dupes-census] is stamped 2/2/32, the census reading after the burn-down (5/5/52 before it), naming its two residual groups: agent_policy.human_approves / human_approves_spine, kept as deliberate (D-009), and check_trajectory.read_rows / gen_release_checklist.load_csv, which are NOT deliberate but deferred: the spec orders that pair to wait on WI-817, which retires the non-TOML carriers and may delete one or both readers.

Alternative passed over

Keep the stamp at 0/0/0 and accept a standing census WARN (2/2/32 over a 0/0/0 baseline) on every run until WI-817 removes or merges the CSV pair and the deliberate pair is merged or allow-listed; or merge the two held-status predicates now to shrink the residual to the deferred pair.

Reversal cost

Three numbers and a comment block in docs/stack.ini.

Why not escalated

Not settled by the builder: this goes to the independent adjudicator. The case against it: the Done-when asks for a census reading of '0/0/0, or the remaining deliberate groups only', and for docs/stack.ini [dupes-census] to be 're-stamped down by hand'; the baseline's own convention is downward-only. Measured against the committed stamp, 0/0/0 -> 2/2/32 is a raise, and the CSV pair is deferred rather than deliberate, so the reading is not 'the remaining deliberate groups only'. The case for it: the committed 0/0/0 was stale, below the 5/5/52 the census actually read before this row (the drift the research's section 7 found), so the burn-down itself moves the reading down 5/5/52 -> 2/2/32; a stamp below the reading WARNs on every run over two named, explained residuals, which is a warning nobody acts on. The census is warn-only either way (D-7), so the choice changes only whether that WARN stands until WI-817.

D-002high riskdocs/decisions/wi-821.toml

Decided

trace.if_note_advisories is the shared trace_text.cite_advisories sweep over the IF reason cells, and its output is the former copy's to the byte ('states the seam and its standing reason', with its closing period): the engine takes the finding's sentence as a value (a str.format template, default trace_text.CITE_MESSAGE, unchanged for the spine and off-spine tiers), and the IF caller passes trace.IF_CITE_MESSAGE.

Alternative passed over

Let the IF advisory take the shared engine's sentence ('states the system', no closing period), a visible output change; or give the tier spec a noun field, which alone cannot restore the closing period.

Reversal cost

One keyword parameter on trace_text.cite_advisories and one module constant in trace.py.

Why not escalated

The Done-when says behaviour is unchanged, so the former wording is kept rather than migrated: tests/test_rule_sync.py pins it verbatim (IF-101, 'Minted 2026-08-15.'). The sentence is data a caller passes, not a mode flag switching behaviour: the sweep (rows, cells, tokens, the token-scoped exception list) stays one loop. Recorded high-risk because it adds a parameter to a shared engine for one caller.

D-001high riskdocs/decisions/wi-822.toml

Decided

The coordinator's call C2: the lease refusals (draining; held by another session; no lease held) apply to every claim route EXCEPT the live dispatcher's (claim(..., dispatch_lock_held=True), the unattended loop, which has its own protection). integrate.claim calls coordinator_guard.claim_refusal first, under if not dispatch_lock_held.

Alternative passed over

Apply the guard to the dispatcher's claims too, or only to the CLI route.

Reversal cost

One condition in integrate.claim and its pinning tests.

Why not escalated

The coordinator made the call in the build prompt. The guard protects an interactive Claude Code coordinator; the unattended loop is a separate path the owner is testing elsewhere, and its dispatcher holds the dispatch lock for its process lifetime. Risk: a hand claim made while the guard is on now needs the lease, so a claim from a plain terminal (no CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID) refuses until the owner releases the lease or the dial is 0.

D-003high riskdocs/decisions/wi-822.toml

Decided

The claim identifies its caller by the CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID environment variable Claude Code 2.1.285 sets for a Bash tool's children. A claim whose caller names no session (a plain terminal, or a version that stops setting it) is refused as not the holder while the guard is on.

Alternative passed over

Have the PreToolUse hook record the last calling session for the claim to read, or deny the claim's Bash call in the hook.

Reversal cost

Replace one lookup in claim_refusal; the refusal ladder is unchanged.

Why not escalated

The spec requires a non-holder's claim to refuse; the environment variable is the one carrier of the caller's identity that reaches a subprocess without a command-spelling rule (round 1's MAJOR). It is version-dependent, which the spec says to treat as a claim. A subagent's Bash shares its parent's session id (observed in this build), so a coordinator's own subagent can claim, which matches the coordinator's authority.

D-001high riskdocs/decisions/wi-823.toml

Decided

This lane's reviews ran on Codex gpt-6-luna at high effort, not gpt-6.1-sol, which the Codex account signed in for the overnight run does not offer (coordinator-2026-10-10 D-017). Luna is a fresh, cross-family reviewer of Opus-built work.

Alternative passed over

Hold the lane until an account offering Sol is signed in, or use a fresh independent Opus reviewer (allowed only after two hours of Codex unavailability, and same-family).

Reversal cost

Low: an overrule re-runs the final gate with Sol; the lane's files do not change.

Why not escalated

The owner is away overnight; the substitution keeps a fresh session from a different model family.

D-002high riskdocs/decisions/wi-823.toml

Decided

Gate 002's only finding (W823F1, K4: a RESYNC entry for the render-dashboard-critique skill) was contested by the coordinator and DISMISSED as refuted by dispute sitting 003 (the skill is scope: this-repo, never materialized downstream). The lane lands on gate 002 without another full-lane round: no file under review changed after the gate (only review records were added), so a second gate would review the same tree. This follows the 2026-10-09 leg-02 precedent (coordinator D-001 of that day), which also awaits the owner.

Alternative passed over

Run one more fresh full-lane round over the unchanged tree before landing.

Reversal cost

Low: an overrule runs one more full-lane round over the landed change; any finding becomes a follow-up row.

Why not escalated

D-001high riskdocs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

The kit's shipped inert Claude hook config (agent-hooks/claude.settings.json, copied by bootstrap as .claude/settings.json.example) now registers the coordinator guard's hook on its eight events, and dev-setup's consented switch merges only the guard's hook groups into .claude/settings.json. The spec's premise that the kit already shipped them inert was wrong: the guard's registration and the relaunch launchers were this repository's own tooling (README row and the WI-822 RESYNC entry: 'not scaffolded').

Alternative passed over

Ship no guard hooks and have dev-setup offer nothing in a scaffold (part D reduced to this repo), or merge the whole example (the subagent gate and the Stop hook too).

Reversal cost

Low: drop the eight groups from the shipped example and the hooks subcommand; adopters who switched them on remove them from .claude/settings.json.

Why not escalated

Part D and its RESYNC line ('dev-setup now offers to switch on the coordinator's hooks') only make sense if the kit ships them; merging only the guard's groups keeps the opt-in to what the spec names. The relaunch launchers stay unshipped, so in a scaffold the hooks act on the blackout window (and on the context guard only if an adopter also supplies launchers), which the README states.

D-004high riskdocs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

Inside the window the hooks deny every SendMessage from the main session, not only one that resumes a subagent, and treat as the main session any call without agent_id (no lease is needed, so they act with the guard off).

Alternative passed over

Inspect SendMessage's tool_input to deny only a message addressed to a subagent; or deny only the lease holder's calls.

Reversal cost

Low: one entry in LAUNCH_TOOLS and its test.

Why not escalated

The hook input carries no field this code can rely on to tell a subagent target from another; every SendMessage target is a model that would work inside the window, so the broader denial keeps usage minimal (ruling (a)). With the guard off there is no lease to name a holder.

D-005high riskdocs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

The dispatcher holds its claim inside the window at the tick (dispatch._blackout_hold: an idle station waits the window out with the banner; with lanes live it claims nothing and lets them finish), in addition to integrate.claim refusing the dispatcher's claim. Without the hold a refused claim would end the run fatally.

Alternative passed over

Treat a refused claim's exit code as a hold inside the dispatcher instead of asking the window at the tick.

Reversal cost

Low: one function in dispatch.py.

Why not escalated

Ruling (i) refuses the claim; how the dispatcher waits is implementation, and asking the one window function at the tick keeps the claim's refusal the boundary without decoding exit codes.

D-001high riskdocs/decisions/wi-835.toml

Decided

The sign-in probe covers OPENAI as well as ANTHROPIC (coordinator decision): codex login status runs under CODEX_HOME set to the dedicated home. Probed on this box's codex-cli 0.160.1 (the spec named 0.160.0): a signed-out home writes Not logged in and exits 1, a signed-in one writes Logged in using ChatGPT and exits 0, both on stderr after any WARNING lines (an empty temporary home also printed a PATH-alias warning). The reader takes exit 0 with a Logged in line as signed-in, a non-zero exit with a Not logged in line as missing, and anything else (another wording, a missing subcommand, a failure, a timeout) as unknown, which refuses.

Alternative passed over

Probe ANTHROPIC only, as the spec's Done-when names only claude auth status, leaving the loop's retained OpenAI adjudications to launch into whatever their dedicated home holds.

Reversal cost

One row of session_service.SIGNIN_PROBES and its reader, and two parametrised test cases.

Why not escalated

The coordinator decided it in the build prompt: the dial at 55 turns the dedicated home on for the loop's OpenAI adjudicator routes too, and without a probe such a route would launch into an empty home. The codex wording was probed on the installed CLI rather than guessed, and an answer the reader does not recognise is unknown, never signed in.

D-002high riskdocs/decisions/wi-835.toml

Decided

The refusal sits in session_service.plan_keep, after the dial and class check and before keep_for, so both adjudication routes pass it and a refused call takes no lease, creates no home and writes no record. The keep-warm ping is not probed: it only resumes a session already minted under the home, and a ping that fails retires that session under the existing rule.

Alternative passed over

Refuse in session_service.act for any call whose keep carries a dedicated home, which also covers the keep-warm ping, but runs after keep_for has taken the lease and would route the refusal through keep_abandon, retiring a healthy session.

Reversal cost

Move one call (require_signin) and add a probe to take_warm_lease's caller.

Why not escalated

The Done-when scopes the refusal to a launch 'whose keep needs the sign-in' on either route, and both adjudication routes reach the keep only through plan_keep. Probing before the lease is what makes the refusal touch nothing; keep-warm is off in this repo (keepwarm_minutes = 0). Recorded high-risk because it leaves the ping unprobed.

D-003high riskdocs/decisions/wi-835.toml

Decided

With the probe reading this machine's dedicated ANTHROPIC home as signed in, docs/process.toml [adjudicator] context_reset_pct is set to 55 (owner ruling (b)), knowing the probe reads the dedicated OPENAI home as missing: from this commit, a loop adjudication of a retained class (disposition, amendment, red-tc, and first-approval since the owner's D-007 overrule) drawn on an OpenAI route is refused before launch and the run stops needing a human, until the owner signs in under out/adjudicator/home/openai.

Alternative passed over

Hold the dial at 0 until both families' homes are signed in; or narrow retention to ANTHROPIC routes, which no dial supports today.

Reversal cost

One number in docs/process.toml and the WI-802 line.

Why not escalated

The build prompt orders the dial set once the ANTHROPIC probe reads signed in, and says the OpenAI result is expected to be missing and changes nothing. The refusal is the owner's no-fallback rule doing its job: the alternative to refusing is launching into an empty home. Recorded high-risk because it can stop an unattended run until the OpenAI sign-in is made.

D-002high riskdocs/decisions/wi-838.toml

Decided

A mint's bookkeeping lands only while the route's record still carries that call's own lease (holder equal to the keep's, expired or not); any other holder, or no lease, or no record, returns "store moved on". Before WI-838 a mint refused only when another call held a live lease on a live (not retired) record. Round 1 of this work item widened that to a live lease on any record, which still let a late first mint replace a replacement that had completed and released its lease (Codex Sol's round-1 MAJOR, reproduced red). The own-lease rule closes both orderings: a first call overruns its lease, a second takes the expired lease over and mints, and the late first call never replaces that record, whether the second is still in flight or already bookkept.

Alternative passed over

Keep a liveness rule (refuse only while another call's lease is live), which lets the late first mint replace a completed replacement, generation 1 -> 2; or compare generations, which needs the keep to carry the record's state at the lease.

Reversal cost

One condition in session_keep._landing and two TC-329 tests.

Why not escalated

The spec's gap is exactly 'the second bookkeeping replaces the first session's record', and LLR-270 promises that a record another session replaced is left alone. Every mint takes its own lease in keep_for before it launches, so the rule changes no normal path: the first mint, the remint over a retired record, the same-artifact retire and the drained-session remint all land on their own lease (the existing session_keep, session_service and coordinator_adjudicate tests pass unchanged). Recorded high-risk because it changes older behaviour at the edges: a mint whose record was deleted, made unreadable, or retaken by another call while it ran now records nothing, where before it wrote a fresh record. Such a session is simply not retained, and the next call mints.

D-002high riskdocs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

The hold points are (a) the loop's next BUILD dispatch, asked from worker_endstate before a build or rework session (a review session is never held, and an adjudication row is never held), returning EXIT_NEEDS_HUMAN with label HELD; (b) the merge slot, a rung in _merge_refusal after the close records; (c) a hand close, a new pre-commit step done-when-blessed running integrate.py done-when-hold on a staged commit that moves a spec out of docs/work/active/<branch>/ into complete/partial/cancelled. The claimed text is read at the lane's integration base in the lane (worker base / agent_common.default_base), at trunk HEAD in the merge slot, and for a hand close at default_base when committed on the lane's own branch, else at HEAD.

Alternative passed over

Hold in route_session or run_iteration (both over the complexity budget, 37 and 15), or hold every session including reviews; or read the claimed text at the claim commit everywhere.

Reversal cost

Three call sites, each one line into kitlib.done_when.lane_hold, plus one check.py step tuple.

Why not escalated

The spec names the two consumers (next build dispatch, close and merge); the build prompt names these code points. Recorded high-risk because a hand close committed on trunk after a squash of the lane reads trunk's (already edited) copy as the claim and so passes: that path relies on the lane-side close commit having been judged by the same hook, and on intake's safety net.

D-004high riskdocs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Every Done-when verdict outcome covers the text it names: CLARITY, BLESSED and SUCCESSOR all release the hold. A SUCCESSOR verdict drafts the unblessed scope in a ## Dispositions section of the verdict file, and the merge-time intake mints those drafts (a SUCCESSOR verdict without a draft refuses the mint); the lane's text stands, never reversed.

Alternative passed over

Let SUCCESSOR keep the lane held until the owner rules; or have the coordinator file the successor by hand.

Reversal cost

Drop SUCCESSOR from kitlib.done_when.OUTCOMES' covering set and remove intake._successor_drafts.

Why not escalated

The spec: a moved scope the adjudicator would not bless is drafted as a successor, never a reversal. A lane never mints (R1), so the merge mints, as it already does for an adjudication row's Dispositions. Recorded high-risk because a lane whose scope was narrowed can then close on the narrowed text, with the dropped scope carried only by the minted successor; any verdict file under docs/reviews/ is read, so like every adjudication verdict it is trusted as written by its session.

D-006high riskdocs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

tests/test_adjudicate_brief.py's producer assertion (every routed brief is declared by a mint source) now exempts combined and asserts instead that every kind it composes is declared. The merge-time goalposts row now declares the done-when brief and Adjudicates = <the closed WI>, so done-when has a mint producer, and its brief composes after the merge too (the claim copy read at the newest commit that added the spec under active/).

Alternative passed over

Have intake mint a combined row when one merge raises several kinds; or keep the goalposts row brief-less and exempt done-when too.

Reversal cost

One test line; the goalposts draft's two keys.

Why not escalated

A combined sitting is by design held in the lane before the merge, so no merge mints one. Recorded high-risk because it relaxes a pinned guard, narrowly and with the reason in the test.

D-002high riskdocs/decisions/wi-842.toml

Decided

A hand-back is refused while the holder's OWN relaunch request (relaunch.json naming the calling session) is pending, telling it to end the session so its relaunched successor takes the lease; the lease and the request are left unchanged. A request left by a previous holder (one that requested a relaunch and was then released by the owner) does not block the current holder's hand-back and is left in place, untouched: the existing session_end path already refuses it as foreign (moving it to .refused and recording relaunch-refused) at a later holder's exit, and a later holder's own request-relaunch replaces it. An unreadable request file does not block either. (Round 2: Codex Sol round-1 MAJOR, a previous holder's request stranded the current holder's lease.)

Alternative passed over

(a) Let the hand-back free the lease whatever request is on file, which silently cancels the holder's own requested relaunch; (b) block on any request file (round 1), which strands the current holder's lease behind a crashed predecessor's request; (c) move a superseded request aside to .refused inside the hand-back, a second refusal path beside session_end's.

Reversal cost

One helper (_own_request_pending) and its check in hand_back, and two tests.

Why not escalated

The spec makes the hand-back the close-out's last act 'unless it requested a relaunch', so the holder's own request and its hand-back are exclusive; the coordinator's round-2 direction scopes the block to the current holder's request and asks for one code path for superseded requests, which leaving it to session_end keeps. Recorded high-risk because it is a refusal the spec does not name and it leaves a stale request file until a later exit or request replaces it.

D-001high riskdocs/decisions/wi-846.toml

Decided

Competing credentials (Sol round 1, MAJOR 1): for a token family the launch environment is composed, not overlaid. The ambient higher-precedence credential sources the environment can carry (the cloud-provider switches, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) are dropped and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN added; a route that declares one of them, or whose template carries --bare, is refused before launch. Settings-file sources (apiKeyHelper, settings env blocks, a managed gateway sign-in) are not handled, and the bound is stated in the IF-282 contract and the session-protocol text; apiKeySource from the init event is not recorded.

Alternative passed over

Refuse any launch whose ambient environment carries a competing credential; or read the init event's apiKeySource after launch and fail the call when it is not the token; or leave the overlay as built.

Reversal cost

One composition helper and its tuple; a later row can add the post-launch apiKeySource check.

Why not escalated

Composing the credential set makes the ambient case unrepresentable, which is the owner's rule (fix the single point of failure, no fallback). A route's own declared competitor is a contradiction to refuse, not to strip silently. The settings-file residue has no pre-launch remedy short of dropping project settings the kit relies on. Recorded high-risk because a settings-file credential can still outrank the token silently.

D-002high riskdocs/decisions/wi-846.toml

Decided

Echoed token (Sol round 1, MAJOR 2): the captured stream and the live line echo are redacted by the token's exact value at the one call boundary (session_service.act), before final text, usage, metrics, the raw run-log and the record read it. The launched CLI's own transcript in the dedicated home and the model's tool subprocesses (which inherit the environment, and the route skips permission prompts) are left outside this row: neither CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB nor the undocumented file-descriptor transport is used, and the bound is stated in the IF-282 contract.

Alternative passed over

Set CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB for the retained launch (its interaction with the route's permission mode is unverified); or pass the token by file descriptor (undocumented, POSIX-only in Python); or file an open item before landing.

Reversal cost

One redaction helper; a later row can add either transport once verified.

Why not escalated

Exact-value redaction is genuine trust-boundary validation: the child can print what it holds. The residue is no wider than before this row, when the same model in the same home could read the OAuth credential file. Recorded high-risk because the token sits in an environment a permission-skipping model can read.

spine-authoring keeps its landed WI-849 wording where the reviewed draft predates it: the 'Authoring is not approving' preamble (the act is an independent adjudicator's, taken in the authoring lane or on trunk) and the §6 cell-hygiene line ('the adjudication (the preamble above ...)'), so only the description's lane clause, the 'Three ways a spine grows' section and references/in-lane.md land from the draft. in-lane.md's held CLARITY line keeps today's mechanism (an independent sitting rules CLARITY in its verdict and the act names that file in --verdict) and names no WI-851: WI-851 has not landed and owns that line's change in its own Done-when, and a kit skill that ships to adopters must not cite this repo's row ids.

D-002high riskdocs/decisions/wi-858.toml

Decided

Review 001 F1 (a replayed bookkeep marker freed a newer holder's lease) is fixed by binding consumption to the per-call lease, not by a separate consumed-marker set: a call's observation lands only while the record still carries that call's own lease (a resumed call's, only on the live session and generation it resumed), and landing drops the lease in the same whole-record write, so a replay finds no lease of its publisher and is inert. Reversal cost

Why not escalated

The fix makes the replay unrepresentable at the store boundary, the reviewer's stated aim; the next Sol round judges it.

D-003high riskdocs/decisions/wi-880.toml

Decided

Sitting 001's third return (a [run] line's bare python3 is not the menu interpreter on Windows) is answered by narrowing, not by code: LLR-047 and SR-046's new clause state that bare python is exact on every platform and python3 only on POSIX, where a Windows interpreter's directory has no python3. The RESYNC entry and run_menu's docstring say a line meant for Windows declares python. TC-047 drives python3 on POSIX, the platforms the narrowed claim covers.

Alternative passed over

Make python3 exact on Windows with a per-launch directory holding a python3 shim.

Reversal cost

Medium: a later row could add a Windows mechanism and widen the claim back; the narrowed text would then be amended.

Why not escalated

Every Windows mechanism found is worse than the gap: a batch-file shim (python3.cmd) re-parses %* after cmd has consumed the caret escapes, reopening the WI-227 data-argument contract for a quoted value holding a metacharacter (probed 2026-10-10 on this box: through a python3.cmd shim the trailing value a"&echo INJECTED ran the echo; the direct call kept it one argument), and a copied or linked python3.exe outside the interpreter's directory loses its home (the DLL and a venv's pyvenv.cfg beside it). Correction (sitting 002, 2026-10-10): Windows' official Python install manager does provide a python3 on PATH, so a Windows-run line declaring python3 reaches that manager's default rather than the menu interpreter; the narrowing stands and SR-046 states the platform split outright.

D-001high riskdocs/decisions/wi-881.toml

Decided

A Windows session's tree kill is a job object, not taskkill: the child is created suspended, assigned to its own job, then resumed with ntdll's NtResumeProcess, and a deadline kill terminates the job. On this workstation taskkill /F [/T] /PID times out after about 61 s and kills nothing (the builder's probes, 2026-10-10), so before this change only proc.kill() worked and a grandchild survived every deadline kill. NtResumeProcess is undocumented but long-standing; it is used because Popen discards the child's primary-thread handle, and the documented route (a thread snapshot to find that thread) takes about 1.2 s here. A child that cannot be contained is killed before it runs and the session errors; there is no fallback to an uncontained child. Probed live through the new spawn: node spawning a child, codex --version and claude --version all ran inside the job.

Alternative passed over

Resume through the documented thread-snapshot route (OpenThread plus ResumeThread) at about 1.2 s per spawn, or kill the direct child and walk the process list (1.2 s, and it misses a grandchild whose parent has exited).

Reversal cost

Low: the resume call is one function (_contain_in_job); swapping it for the documented route changes no interface.

Why not escalated

The owner's rule is to fix the single point of failure without a fallback path; the job object does that, and the undocumented call is isolated in one function the full-lane review will judge.

D-002high riskdocs/decisions/wi-881.toml

Decided

Answer sitting 001's first return by bounding the claim, not strengthening the mechanism: SR-238 and LLR-026 promise that every process still in the session's process group (POSIX) or job (Windows) ends. The residual is recorded as a decided gap in SR-238's Rationale: a POSIX descendant that leaves the group (setsid or setpgid), or a process another service starts on the session's behalf outside the job (WMI, the task scheduler, an already-running daemon), is not ended.

Alternative passed over

Strengthen POSIX by tracking descendants instead of the group: a /proc walk on Linux plus a child subreaper, with no equivalent on macOS, or a cgroup, which needs privilege. Each is per-OS code for a descendant that detaches on purpose, and the Windows job has the analogous service-started residual anyway.

Reversal cost

Medium: a later row adds descendant tracking behind _kill_tree and widens SR-238's acceptance; no interface changes.

Why not escalated

The sitting returned it as the coordinator's call. Bounding keeps the claim true to the mechanism, and the residual is written into the row where a reader finds it.

D-004high riskdocs/decisions/wi-881.toml

Decided

Narrow review 002's F1 (a job member created between the handle snapshot and the terminate was never waited on; 12 of 12 trials) is answered by closing the job to new members before the snapshot: _kill_tree sets the job's active-process limit to 1, then snapshots, then terminates, so no process can join after the snapshot (the builder's measurements: 384 creations refused in the gap, 0 unsignalled at return; a refused creation runs no code and holds no inherited pipe). A live member the kill cannot open for SYNCHRONIZE (access denied, told apart from a gone PID by its error code) makes the kill raise after the terminate rather than be read as exited. The cost: a session whose descendants deny their own SYNCHRONIZE right errors at every deadline kill.

Alternative passed over

Re-snapshot after the terminate (not airtight: after a job terminate a member leaves the PID list before it is signalled, 100 of 100), or a completion port (its messages are documented as not guaranteed). For an unopenable member, grant SYNCHRONIZE through the owner's WRITE_DAC right, which rewrites another process's permissions.

Reversal cost

Low: inside _kill_tree's Windows half; no interface changes.

Why not escalated

It closes the reviewed class at its one owner without a fallback path; the unopenable-member cost is loud, and the DACL rewrite waits for a real case.

D-002high riskdocs/decisions/wi-925.toml

D-003high riskdocs/decisions/wi-957.toml

D-008docs/decisions/wi-791.toml

D-002docs/decisions/wi-797.toml

Decided

GLOSSARY.md marks every term whose machinery a later S788 row builds with a visible 'Planned.' label and a 'Today:' line stating what runs in its place, without naming the S788 row ids. Why not escalated

The design says only that the column is allowed. The tier vocabulary's one home is agent_route.TIER_ORDER (CMP-008); importing it here adds an undeclared cross-component edge, and copying it makes a second home. The consumer that applies a child's tier (plan_artifacts, under S788-dual-pickup) reads the cell and is the place to refuse a bad one.

D-005docs/decisions/wi-803.toml

Decided

Excludes: grammar: 'Excludes: <ref>[; <ref>] <sep> <reason>', optionally list-marked or bold, anywhere in the plan, where <sep> is an em dash, an en dash, or a hyphen with whitespace before it. Several refs on one line share the reason. A line with no reason excludes nothing and is a finding; a ref that does not resolve is a finding.

Alternative passed over

Em dash only, as the design writes it; or one ref per line.

Reversal cost

One regex (EXCLUDES_SEP_RE).

Why not escalated

Planner output from either family mixes the three dashes; accepting all three keeps the grammar mechanical without rejecting honest exclusions on punctuation. The design's form (em dash) is the documented one.

D-006docs/decisions/wi-803.toml

Decided

The SR/TC diff's TC set is every TC whose verifies cell names one of the item's sr_refs, of any status, read from docs/test/test-cases.toml. An absent TC registry prints a note and leaves the TC diff empty (no finding); an item with no sr_refs has an empty diff.

Alternative passed over

Restrict to Approved TCs, or fail when the TC registry is absent.

Reversal cost

One filter in verifying_tcs, or one finding in _load_gate.

Why not escalated

Today every live TC is Approved, so a status filter would change nothing here; the absent-registry rule is the one the SR and IF checks already follow (absent means unvalidated, never everything unknown, IF-060's note behaviour).

D-007docs/decisions/wi-803.toml

Decided

The argv surface grows by --item and --findings (one of --goal / --item required; --findings only with --item). That changes IF-152 and IF-153 (the report gains excluded lines and a SINGLE SR/TC diff section), which the README matrix does not list for this row.

Alternative passed over

A second script for the SINGLE gate.

Reversal cost

Low: the flags are additive and --goal runs are unchanged.

Why not escalated

One home for the plan grammar and the coverage stage is the CLAUDE.md consolidation rule; a second script would re-implement the table, ref and cycle checks. The IF-152/IF-153 cell drift is reported to the coordinator for the spine author rather than decided here.

D-001docs/decisions/wi-806.toml

Decided

The rule's universe is acceptance_record.APPROVAL_ACT_CSVS: SR, LLR, TC, SN and the assumptions registry's DA and SUR tiers. A commit writing docs/archive/last_approved/ that also changes an interface, frame or component row is not refused by this rule.

Alternative passed over

Walk every SNAPSHOTTED registry, the three off-spine ones (interfaces, external, components) included, since the copy blesses their text too.

Reversal cost

Widen one argument of _spine_row_sides in _text_changes plus the off-spine tiers' id columns; tests for an IF row beside the act.

Why not escalated

The ruling says 'no spine cell except Status', and APPROVAL_ACT_CSVS is the kit's existing boundary for which tiers an approval act blesses (OUTSIDE_THE_APPROVAL_ACT records the off-spine three as OI-30 D3's, by ruling). Widening past the ruling's word is the owner's call; the gap is named here and in the report.

D-002docs/decisions/wi-806.toml

Decided

Every cell counts, traced cells (Module, CodeSymbol, SN-Refs, ...) included: an act commit carrying a re-pointed traced cell is refused, and the re-point lands in the text commit before it.

Alternative passed over

Judge only the approved half of split_changed_cells, letting traced re-points ride the act as 'traced-cell refreshes stay cheap' did.

Reversal cost

Filter _text_changes through spine_cell_class; one line and one test.

Why not escalated

Risk 6 reads 'change no spine cell except Status'. The cost is one extra commit when a re-point and an act coincide; the snapshot copies traced cells byte for byte, so they are text the act blesses.

D-003docs/decisions/wi-806.toml

Decided

A merge commit (a lane's refresh, or a merge in progress at the hook) is judged by what NEITHER parent carried: a record path, cell or row counts only when it differs from every parent.

Alternative passed over

Judge every commit against its first parent only, as the ruling-sync rung does.

Reversal cost

Pass parents[:1] in commit_text_then_act_lines and drop MERGE_HEAD from the staged bases.

Why not escalated

First-parent only would refuse every lane whose refresh merges in trunk's own text commit and act commit together, which the rule exists to require, so it would block the two-commit form it mandates. The held-status rung already judges a merge this way (merge_status_moves); an evil merge's own changes are still caught.

D-005docs/decisions/wi-806.toml

Decided

A root commit, and the staged tree before the first commit, are not judged: there is no earlier commit the text could have been read in.

Alternative passed over

Judge a root commit against the empty tree, refusing a first commit that both adds rows and seeds the record.

Reversal cost

Use _empty_tree as the base in two places.

Why not escalated

The ruling-sync rule answers a root commit the same way; a first commit carrying a seeded record is a bootstrap shape the separation cannot improve.

D-006docs/decisions/wi-806.toml

Decided

The amend-plus-flip allowance retires in code as well as in text: refresh_ledger no longer short-circuits a flipped row and _unattested_rows no longer subtracts flips. Behaviour is unchanged, because a flipped row's copy reads below approval and is never absorbed; a flip now only puts its registry in the act's scope. The refusal offers two ways forward (re-attest after the text commit, or revert).

Alternative passed over

Edit only the docstrings and refusal text, leaving the redundant continue and subtraction.

Reversal cost

Restore two lines.

Why not escalated

Context names the executable allowance as retiring; verified that it is already dead (the flip clause can only fire when the copy reads below approval, which the next clause skips anyway), so removing it changes no outcome and leaves no code claiming the retired doctrine.

D-007docs/decisions/wi-806.toml

Decided

One home per shared stage: acceptance_record._commit_parents (the commit-object parent reader) and integrate._each_lane_commit (the per-lane-commit walk) are extracted and shared by the ruling-sync and text-then-act rules. Module sizes: check.py 1259 -> 1299 and integrate.py 1531 -> 1552 re-stamped with reasons; acceptance_record.py stays under the 1000-line threshold by moving the SQUASH_MSG parse to check.py.

Alternative passed over

Copy the ruling-sync walk and parent reader into the new rule, or put the rule in its own new module.

Reversal cost

Inline the two helpers back.

Why not escalated

CLAUDE.md's consolidate rule. A new module would add layering and bootstrap census entries for about seventy lines that belong beside the mirror rule's two-tree reads.

D-008docs/decisions/wi-806.toml

Decided

The merge-slot rung runs after the ruling sync and before the review-scope rung, so a lane failing both the ruling sync and this rule is named for the ruling sync first.

Alternative passed over

Run it beside the approval-act rung, ahead of held-status.

Reversal cost

Move one call in _merge_refusal.

Why not escalated

Both are per-commit rules over the same walk; order only decides which refusal a lane failing two rules sees first.

D-002docs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

The owner vocabulary is exact and case-sensitive: only the strings "confirmed" and "overruled" are recognized; "Confirmed", a padded word, true or 1 are format findings and read as not yet seen.

Alternative passed over

Compare trimmed and case-folded, as WI-790's reviewed key did.

Reversal cost

One line in owner_state plus the parametrized test's cases.

Why not escalated

The spec says the two values are the only recognized values; the migrator writes the exact word, and a closed exact vocabulary leaves no question of which spellings count.

D-003docs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

Any entry still carrying the retired reviewed key reads as not yet seen, whatever its owner key says (owner = "confirmed" plus reviewed = true is listed under Decisions to review, confirmed count 0), and the key is a format finding. The overrule coupling reads the owner key as written: owner = "overruled" beside reviewed still owes its citing work item at the commit.

Alternative passed over

Read such an entry by owner alone (the round-1 build: owner = "confirmed" plus reviewed reads as confirmed); or let the retired key also suppress the coupling, so the coupling and the surface read one way.

Reversal cost

One condition in review_queue and the parametrized test's confirmed case; one in _overruled_ids for the coupling.

Why not escalated

Round 1 read the entry by owner alone, which the review showed contradicts the spec's first Done-when bullet: the retired key is a format finding AND reads as not yet seen. The coupling keeps the owner key as written because a stale key must never let an overrule skip its work (fail closed), the same reasoning as D-008's blank note.

D-006docs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

Overruled entries render inside section 4 of open-items.html under their own sub-heading 'Overruled - acted on by work', after the not-yet-seen cards, each with an 'Acted on by' field naming every citing work item and its state folder (open or archived), or 'no work item cites this entry'. They stay listed for good.

Alternative passed over

A fifth section after 'Decisions to review'; or drop an overruled entry from the page once its citing work item closes.

Reversal cost

Low: a render change in gen_open_items.decisions_block and the section-order test.

Why not escalated

The section-order test pins 'Decisions to review' as the last section (LLR-118), and the spec asks only for 'their own heading'; keeping every overrule listed is the plain reading of 'never disappears silently'.

D-007docs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

The migrator is a new script, scripts/migrate_decisions.py, over a pure kitlib.decisions.migrate_text: each word of the old reviewed vocabulary that read as reviewed becomes owner = "confirmed" in the same place, a not-reviewed word is dropped, a reviewed key beside an existing owner key is dropped, and a value outside the old vocabulary is left in place and named (still a finding). It rewrites complete top-level assignments only, found by a scanner that tracks TOML string and bracket state, never a string's contents; a rewritten or dropped assignment keeps its trailing comment (a dropped one leaves the comment on its own line); it re-parses the result and refuses (ValueError, the record left untouched and named) unless only the verdict keys changed, comparing NaN as equal to NaN. --check reports without writing.

Alternative passed over

Rewrite only the literal true and false and leave every word form; scan physical lines (the round-1 build, which rewrote a reviewed line inside a multiline note and left a multiline value half-replaced); or fold the migrator into an existing script such as migrate_carrier.py.

Reversal cost

Low for the vocabulary (one helper); moving the CLI means one argparse block and the RESYNC_PACK pointer.

Why not escalated

The spec names reviewed = true and reviewed = false; the old vocabulary's other words meant the same thing under WI-790, so carrying them is the same migration, and guessing an unrecognized value is left to a person. A dedicated script keeps migrate_carrier.py to its one job; it needs its own spine row, listed for the row author.

D-008docs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

An overruled entry with a blank review note is a format finding but still reads as overruled: it leaves the review queue for the overruled heading, and its commit is still held to the citing-row coupling.

Alternative passed over

Read an overrule with no note as not yet seen until the note is written.

Reversal cost

One condition in review_queue.

Why not escalated

The spec makes the blank note a format finding and says nothing about how it reads; reading the key as written keeps the coupling on the commit that sets it, so a missing note never lets an overrule skip its work item.

D-009docs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

The status snapshot's 'Decisions to review' count is unchanged: it counts entries not yet seen only, not overruled ones.

Alternative passed over

Add an overruled count line to the snapshot.

Reversal cost

One line in traj_status._open_item_lines and a test.

Why not escalated

The spec changes the owner surface, not the snapshot; an overrule is already coupled to a work item that the snapshot's queue shows.

D-010docs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

One run-name alphabet serves the record path and the citation reader: the characters a run name cannot keep are exactly what git refuses in any branch name, one character at a time (the ASCII control characters, space and DEL, and ~ ^ : ? * [ and backslash), matched as an explicit ASCII class, plus the two delimiters a branch may carry, '/' and '#' (D-013). record_path maps '/' to '-', exactly as on trunk, and raises ValueError for a run name carrying any other excluded character ('#' or one git refuses); no other character is rewritten. The citation pattern matches every character the alphabet keeps, so owner+cleanup, owner@cleanup and owner<U+00A0>cleanup records are cited as written. Against trunk's record_path, which mapped only '/', every path record_path returns is unchanged; a name carrying '#' now has no path. (Corrected in round 4, Sol round 3 MAJOR 2: the round-3 build matched Python's Unicode whitespace class, which git does not refuse, so owner<U+00A0>cleanup and owner-cleanup collided on one path. Corrected in round 5, dispute 1 ruling: round 4 mapped '#' to '-' as well, so owner#cleanup wrote owner-cleanup's file; it is refused instead.)

Alternative passed over

Normalize in record_path instead: map every character outside the word characters, '.' and '-' to '-', so owner+cleanup writes owner-cleanup.toml and the citation pattern keeps its round-2 class.

Reversal cost

Low: swap the rewrite in record_path and the class in the citation pattern; the alphabet test pins all three outcomes (mapped, refused, kept) against git. A lane already carrying a record named with + or @ would need it renamed.

Why not escalated

Sol's round-2 MAJOR 2 asks only that producer and reader share one alphabet; widening the reader keeps every record name a lane may already carry valid, where normalizing would move them, and it avoids two branches (owner+x, owner@x) colliding on one file.

D-011docs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

Every path list the ruling sync reads is read NUL-delimited (git's -z) through one reader, acceptance_record._git_paths: the diff's changed paths, which the open-item sync and the overrule sync share, and _tree_specs' listing of each tree's work-item specs, which predates this lane and is the open-item sync's. The spine scan's own changed-path read (_spine_revs) is left as it is.

Alternative passed over

Fix only the overrule sync's filter (decode git's quoted form there); or route every raw path listing in acceptance_record through the reader, _spine_revs included.

Reversal cost

Low: the reader is one function and three call sites.

Why not escalated

The build prompt directs the fix at the one shared reader, and names the open-item sync's use of it in scope as the same defect class. _spine_revs compares fixed ASCII registry paths, so quoting cannot hide one there; changing it is outside this row and is reported as a separate finding.

D-012docs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

To bring acceptance_record.py back under the module-size ratchet's 1000-SLOC threshold (1051 after this lane; WI-806 had left it at 999), the overrule sync moved to kitlib/decisions.py (_open_spec, _owed_overrules, overrule_sync_lines, now taking the diff's paths and two text readers, so the module still reads no git itself), and the ruling sync's two git reads moved to kitlib/git.py (git_paths, from _git_paths; git_show and UnreadableBlob, from _show and _UnreadableBlob). acceptance_record keeps one alias for each read and calls overrule_sync_lines from ruling_sync_lines with readers over the parent and resulting tree. Behaviour unchanged; it measures 998.

Alternative passed over

Move the whole ruling sync (WI-790's open-item arm and this lane's overrule arm) into a module of its own, which the acceptance record's boundary sentence does not cover; or re-stamp a 1051 baseline.

Reversal cost

Low: move the five functions and one class back and drop the aliases; the tests call the public staged and commit functions and do not change.

Why not escalated

The ratchet's rule is decompose, never bump, and the coordinator named the overrule coupling and the git path reader as the candidates. Moving the whole ruling sync would change the module cell of LLR-298, an approved row outside this lane, so the move is kept to code this lane owns plus _show, which no approved row's code_symbol names. At 998 the module has 2 SLOC of headroom, so the next feature that grows it must decompose again; the whole-ruling-sync move is the larger cut left for that.

D-015docs/decisions/wi-818.toml

Decided

The merge slot's absent-record refusal text moved from integrate._decision_record_refusal to a new pure function beside owed, kitlib.decisions.missing_record_refusal(mode, run), which also composes the refusal for a run name record_path refuses (naming the run and record_path's ValueError text, ending '; nothing was merged'). The rung keeps the read and the dial: it catches the ValueError around record_path and the git read, treats it as an absent record, and returns missing_record_refusal when owed() holds. The absent-record wording is byte-identical to before.

Alternative passed over

Keep both refusal texts in integrate.py, as the dispute 1 ruling sketches, and re-stamp integrate.py's module-size baseline up by about four SLOC.

Reversal cost

Low: inline the function back into the rung and drop it from IF-256's contract text and LLR-283's code_symbol.

Why not escalated

integrate.py sat exactly on its module-size baseline (1554 SLOC) and the coordinator's rule is decompose, never bump. The refusal is a pure function of the dial and the run name, the module already owns owed() and the session note that announces the refusal, and the move takes integrate.py down to 1551 (re-stamped down). Behaviour is the ruling's: the branch and the exception's text are named and nothing is merged. The row author owes LLR-283 code_symbol and detail and IF-256 data the new function.

D-003docs/decisions/wi-821.toml

Decided

The plan-table walk's home is kitlib.registry.plan_table_rows (a declared shared-kernel module), which plan_coverage.parse_plan and plan_artifacts.parse_plan_wis both call, each picking its own cells.

Alternative passed over

plan_artifacts imports plan_coverage.parse_plan directly.

Reversal cost

Move one function and its two helpers back into plan_coverage and import it from plan_artifacts.

Why not escalated

plan_artifacts is CMP-008 and plan_coverage CMP-006, so a direct import is a new cross-component edge owing a new IF row and a Contract declaration in plan_coverage's header. An edge into a declared kernel module (docs/kernel-modules-allow) is exempt, and kitlib.registry is already the work registry's read home that plan_coverage imports.

D-004docs/decisions/wi-821.toml

Decided

The leading-docstring test's one home is the stdlib's ast.get_docstring, read by check_stubs.stub_kind and check_dupes_census._stripped_body. check_complexity keeps its own _is_docstring, which _wrapped_def uses to drop every string statement in a body, not only the leading one.

Alternative passed over

Export one _is_docstring predicate from check_complexity (or check_stubs) and import it in the other two.

Reversal cost

One helper and two call sites.

Why not escalated

ast.get_docstring answers exactly the copies' question for a function node (an Expr whose value is a str Constant, first in the body), so no kit predicate is needed for it. check_complexity's remaining use is a different question; changing it to the leading docstring would change a complexity score in the case where a decorator body carries a second string.

D-005docs/decisions/wi-821.toml

Decided

frame_rules binds the shipped kitlib.spine.seam_endpoints under its local name _entries, and seam_endpoints' docstring now says it is the carrier's one list-cell split.

Alternative passed over

Rename seam_endpoints to a neutral name (list_entries) across its callers.

Reversal cost

A rename across three call sites and a RESYNC entry.

Why not escalated

seam_endpoints is a shipped kitlib name RESYNC_PACK already documents; renaming it would force a downstream migration for no behaviour. Binding under a local name is the house pattern (plan_artifacts._split_tokens = kitlib.spine.refs).

D-006docs/decisions/wi-821.toml

Decided

The 'two _clips' are read as the one-line width clips (hats._clip and intake._clip, with check_trajectory._clip_title as a third copy); kitlib.spine.clip_line takes text, and each caller keeps its own reading of a missing value (hats and check_trajectory read None as empty, intake as 'None').

Alternative passed over

Unify the None reading on one rule; or read 'two _clips' as the line-count clips in adjudicate_brief and agent_common.

Reversal cost

One function and three one-line callers.

Why not escalated

The research's M2-j0.7 pair is the exact-body width clip. Unifying the None reading would change intake's briefs, where 'None' shows an absent cell. The line-count clips differ in their elision marker ('clipped at N lines' for the author, 'N more lines' for a prompt), so they are different outputs, not copies; left as they are.

D-007docs/decisions/wi-821.toml

Decided

trunk_step.rebase_links lands a fragment through a new public spec_move.expected_rebase(text, old_dir, new_dir), the outbound half's pure oracle beside expected_relink, imported lazily.

Alternative passed over

Import spec_move at trunk_step's module scope, or move the link primitives from spec_move into trunk_step.

Reversal cost

One function in spec_move and the restored 40-line copy in trunk_step.

Why not escalated

spec_move is the link-aware move ritual and owns the per-link decision; the copy in trunk_step was kept only because its first home, the dispatcher, was retired. A module-scope import roughly doubles trunk_step's import cost (about 60 ms, agent_common's chain) for every importer of it; the lazy import follows trunk_step's own _plan_artifacts idiom. Both modules are CMP-008, so no seam row is owed.

D-008docs/decisions/wi-821.toml

Decided

check_dupes_census.py stays this repository's sensor only; it is not added to the bootstrap MAPPING, and its project-trajectory/mapping-source-exclusions reason now says so.

Alternative passed over

Map it into scaffolds with a RESYNC entry.

Reversal cost

One MAPPING row, a [step:] line in the template stack.ini and a RESYNC entry.

Why not escalated

It measures project-trajectory/scripts/ against this repo's own baseline. In an adopter that tree is the copied kit, which the adopter does not edit, so the reading would measure the kit and not their code; pointing it at an adopter's sources is a new feature this row does not ask for.

D-009docs/decisions/wi-821.toml

Decided

agent_policy.human_approves and human_approves_spine stay two functions, as the research judged, and gain a by-value pin in tests/test_rule_sync.py holding them equal over every registry spelling at every dial.

Alternative passed over

Make one call the other, or merge them into one predicate.

Reversal cost

One test, or a two-line merge.

Why not escalated

The research judged the pair deliberate (two contracts, writer side and reader side, on one body), and the row keeps that unless the build finds otherwise. The build found no defect in it. test_rule_sync's rule licenses a second copy of a decision only with a behavioural pin, and none existed.

D-002docs/decisions/wi-822.toml

Decided

The coordinator's call C7: the guard module ships (integrate.claim imports it; dormant at context_guard_pct = 0, the shipped template value). The hook registration (.claude/settings.json) and the relaunch launchers (scripts/coordinator-relaunch.cmd and .sh) are this repo's tooling and do not ship in this row; the builder's recommendation is reported and the coordinator records the decision.

Alternative passed over

Ship the hook registration as an inert example under agent-hooks/ and the launchers beside the module, or keep the module itself out of the shipped scripts.

Reversal cost

Add the two launchers and a settings example to bootstrap's MAPPING with a RESYNC entry; no adopter data migrates.

Why not escalated

The coordinator made the call in the build prompt; the spec leaves shipping to the end of the row.

D-004docs/decisions/wi-822.toml

Decided

An explicit take is a CLI (coordinator_guard.py take) run from the coordinator session: it records the session from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and, when no --transcript is given, the holder's first hook call (not a subagent's) fills the transcript path in. A take of a free lease succeeds; a take of a lease held by another session refuses naming the release; a re-take by the holder changes nothing (it never unlatches).

Alternative passed over

Take at SessionStart for any session started with an environment flag, or derive the transcript path from the projects directory's slug.

Reversal cost

One function and its CLI arm.

Why not escalated

The spec names 'an explicit take' without its mechanism; the CLI keeps the take a deliberate act and adds no second SessionStart path.

D-005docs/decisions/wi-822.toml

Decided

The successor is identified by a random token: SessionEnd writes it into the lease before launching, the launcher passes it to the new session as PT_COORDINATOR_TAKE, and that session's SessionStart hook takes the lease only when the token matches. A mismatched token is recorded as take-refused.

Alternative passed over

Take the lease at the first SessionStart after a launch, whatever session it is.

Reversal cost

The token field and one comparison.

Why not escalated

The spec requires the lease to pass to exactly one successor; any other session starting in the repo at that moment must not take it.

D-006docs/decisions/wi-822.toml

Decided

Exit reasons are an allow-list of the documented SessionEnd reasons other than clear and resume: logout, prompt_input_exit, other. An undocumented reason never launches.

Alternative passed over

A deny-list of clear and resume, launching on any other reason.

Reversal cost

One constant.

Why not escalated

The spec says 'an exit reason, never clear or resume'; an allow-list fails closed on a future reason that is not an exit.

D-007docs/decisions/wi-822.toml

Decided

Unknown occupancy never latches and never refuses on its own: the holder's claim proceeds when no valid usage is readable, and the reading is recorded as unknown with its reason. A reading above the declared window is flagged as a window mismatch and still latches (its percent is over any threshold).

Alternative passed over

Refuse claims while occupancy is unknown.

Reversal cost

One condition in latch_reading.

Why not escalated

Right after a compaction no usage exists until the next reply; refusing then would stop a coordinator at its lowest context. The spec requires unknown never to read as 0%, which holds: unknown is reported as unknown.

D-008docs/decisions/wi-822.toml

Decided

The reminder interval is a constant (REMINDER_EVERY = 20 monitored events), not a dial; the reader reads a 256 KiB tail first and doubles to at most 8 MiB before reporting unknown.

Alternative passed over

Declare the interval and the tail sizes as [coordinator] dials.

Reversal cost

Two keys in both process.toml files and a RESYNC note.

Why not escalated

The spec names exactly two dials (threshold and window) and says 'bounded reminders' without a number; more dials are more adopter surface for no stated need.

D-009docs/decisions/wi-822.toml

Decided

The relaunch launchers run claude with the prompt as one argument: on Windows the .cmd calls coordinator_guard.py exec-claude --prompt-file, so Python quotes the multi-line prompt; the POSIX .sh opens Terminal (macOS) or x-terminal-emulator (elsewhere) and execs claude with the prompt file's text. The SessionEnd handler starts the launcher with a new console (Windows) or a new session (POSIX).

Alternative passed over

Pass the prompt through cmd arguments, or start claude headless.

Reversal cost

Two small launcher files.

Why not escalated

A .cmd cannot quote a multi-line prompt with quotes and percent signs safely, and an interactive coordinator needs a terminal. Risk, untested here: whether a process started from a SessionEnd hook survives Claude Code's exit on every platform (tests stub the launch; no real session was run).

D-010docs/decisions/wi-822.toml

Decided

The primary checkout's out/ lookup and the exclusive-file lock were extracted in place in session_keep (primary_out_dir, dir_lock) and reused rather than copied: store_dir and store_lock now call them, unchanged in behaviour.

Alternative passed over

Copy the git-common-dir lookup and the lock into the guard, or move them into kitlib.

Reversal cost

Inline the two helpers back into store_dir and store_lock.

Why not escalated

The kit enforces one home per shared stage, and the coordinator named session_keep.store_dir as the lookup to follow.

D-011docs/decisions/wi-822.toml

Decided

A detached launch counts as confirmed when the started launcher is still running after LAUNCH_GRACE_SECONDS (5 s) or has exited 0 within it; a non-zero exit within the grace, a missing launcher, or any failure from writing the prompt file to starting the process restores the request, removes the successor token and the prompt file, and is reported (Sol round 1, MAJOR 2). On Windows the launcher keeps the new console's own standard handles (no redirection); the POSIX launcher, which opens its own terminal, keeps its streams on the null device.

Alternative passed over

Treat process creation as the launch (the round-1 build), or wait for the successor's SessionStart take before releasing the request.

Reversal cost

One wait in launch_detached and its constant.

Why not escalated

Sol reproduced both strandings. A launcher that fails (missing claude, bad root) exits at once; one that works keeps running on Windows (claude runs inside it) or exits 0 having opened a terminal on POSIX. Waiting for the successor's take cannot work from SessionEnd, whose session is ending; the take stays the final confirmation, and an untaken lease is the owner's recorded release.

D-014docs/decisions/wi-822.toml

Decided

session_end holds the store lock from the request's acquisition through the successor-token save, the prompt write, the launch and its confirmation, and restores under that same hold, so restoration never reacquires the lock (Sol round 3, MAJOR: a restoration that had to reacquire it raised StoreBusy when another handler held the lock past the ten-second wait, stranding a consumed request and a successor token). The token save joins the launch's try block, so every failure after acquisition takes the one restoration route. Cost: the lock is held for up to LAUNCH_GRACE_SECONDS (5 s) plus the launcher's start; every other guard entry point (a claim, a hook, the successor's SessionStart take) waits on it, and each waits up to ten seconds, so none is refused by the hold alone. The successor's SessionStart take on Windows, which can start inside the grace, is delayed until the hold ends rather than lost.

Alternative passed over

Make restoration lock-free: rename the consumed request back without the lock and leave the successor token to be cleared later; or retry the reacquire with a longer wait.

Reversal cost

Move the launch out of the with-block in session_end and give _restore its own lock again.

Why not escalated

The coordinator asked for one restoration route and named holding the lock as a candidate. A lock-free restoration still needs the lock to clear the successor token (a lease read-modify-write), so it would split restoration into a locked and an unlocked half; a longer retry only moves the threshold at which the request strands. The hold fits inside the waits every other entry point already has (5 s grace against a 10 s wait, and a 120 s stale-lock takeover), and SessionEnd is a once-per-session event.

D-010docs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

Inside an armed blackout window, a main session's Bash or PowerShell command line the hook cannot read (an unclosed quote, $( substitution, backtick substitution or PowerShell here-string) is DENIED, fail-closed, with a reason naming why and asking for the line to be rewritten; outside the window no line is read at all. An unterminated here-document is not unreadable: bash runs it to the end of input, so its body is skipped to the end.

Alternative passed over

Fail open: treat an unreadable line as naming no model CLI and allow it.

Reversal cost

Low: one except clause in coordinator_guard.launch_reason and its three test cases.

Why not escalated

Fail-open would be a second, degenerate reading path beside the one interpretation (the owner's no-fallback rule): a line the hook cannot read is a line it cannot supervise. The cost is small and bounded: an unclosed quote is a syntax error the shell refuses anyway, the denial applies only to the main session and only inside the window, and the reason tells the session what to rewrite. The heredoc and here-string forms the close-down itself uses (writing the handoff, a commit message) are read, not refused, and are pinned in ALLOWED.

D-011docs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

The hook reads a command line through one module, kitlib/shell_line.py (segments), in the tool's dialect: POSIX quoting for the Bash tool and PowerShell's quoting (single quotes with doubled quotes, backtick escapes, here-strings, braces as boundaries) for the PowerShell tool. Command substitutions ($(...), POSIX backticks) are read as further commands; here-document and here-string bodies are data and are not read. The guard keeps only the command-word reading (assignments, grammar words, the timeout and env prefixes, env's split string read through the same module). model_clis reads cmd_template cells through the kit's one template reader (agent_session.split_cmd via agent_common), so a JSON-array template names its CLI.

Alternative passed over

stdlib shlex in punctuation-aware POSIX mode, inside coordinator_guard.py.

Reversal cost

Low: one pure module and its import in coordinator_guard.py.

Why not escalated

shlex's POSIX mode returns a quoted ';' as the same token as the operator ';' (measured: echo ";" claude lexes to ['echo', ';', 'claude']), so it cannot tell a quoted operator from a boundary, which is REVIEW-A F1's own case; it also has no PowerShell mode and does not skip here-document bodies. The lexer is a separate module because coordinator_guard.py would otherwise reach 1105 SLOC, past the 1000-SLOC module ratchet (tests/test_module_size_ratchet.py); it is 929 with the lexer outside it. The new module is tagged to SR-229 / LLR-300; LLR-300's module and code_symbol cells need it added (the spine author's, at the checkpoint).
