D-016docs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

The lane is left committed on its lane, not landed: the session prompt's bound (a lane not SOUND after the dispute ruling and two more full-lane rounds) was reached. After dispute 005, full-lane round 009 found two defects (answered in 8cb21762, narrow round 010 APPROVE, sitting 011) and full-lane round 012 found one MAJOR: a bare run's readiness step (dev-setup -ForRun / --for-run) and the run.* launcher choose their Python interpreters independently, so with an older Python first on PATH and 3.11 installed the step reports the runtime ready and the launcher then starts the menu on the older interpreter, which fails importing tomllib. Not dismissed under the threat model: an older Python first on PATH is an ordinary workstation, not a contrived host. The owed work is recorded in the handoff for the owner.

Alternative passed over

D-017docs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

Answering full-lane round 012 F1, the one interpreter is resolved by the run launcher: each run.* launcher (root and template) runs its candidates (its .venv interpreter, then exactly its dev-setup's own runtime search in the same order: root run.cmd = scripts/dev-setup.ps1's py, python, python3, py -3.13, py -3.12, py -3.11; root run.sh = scripts/dev-setup.sh's python3, python, python3.13, python3.12, python3.11; the templates = their dev-setup templates' py, python, python3 and python3, python; each dev-setup's list lives in one variable, $PyCandidates / PY_CANDIDATES, and no candidate was added, a parity test pinning the four pairs) with one probe that prints sys.executable only at 3.11+, takes the first answer as a concrete executable path, hands it to the readiness operation as -Python / --python (omitted when none answered), and runs the menu on exactly that path. The readiness operation's run tier checks only the handed interpreter (the floor, by running it) and runs the kit's readers on it; it keeps no candidate search of its own, so its exit 0 speaks for the interpreter the menu runs on. The direct and list forms use the same resolution and, with none, exit 1 with the step, without the readiness operation, a prompt or a pause. The launcher's runnability-only choice and its py -3 fall-through are deleted. Because the sets match, whenever a dev-setup check reports a runtime, run resolves one. A runtime installed during a bare run's offers is not the resolved one, so that run still ends with the step, which names what was checked and says to install Python 3.11+ or put an installed one first on PATH, then run again.

Alternative passed over

The readiness operation resolves and reports its interpreter for the launcher to exec (a result file or a second output stream), or the launcher re-resolves after the readiness operation returns.

Reversal cost

Low: the four run.cmd / run.sh launchers' resolution blocks (run.command delegates), the dev-setup candidate variables and the four dev-setup run tiers' handed-interpreter branch, plus their pins in tests/test_run_devsetup.py.

Why not escalated

The direct and list forms must refuse a sub-floor interpreter without running the readiness operation, so a launcher-side resolution is needed anyway; putting the only one there and handing it to the readiness step leaves a single choice. A readiness-side report would need a second channel out of PowerShell and sh (stdout carries the report and the prompts), and a launcher re-resolution after it would be a second choice. Resolving to sys.executable also removes the py-launcher shebang substitution D-008 measured. The trade-off (an install during the run needs a second run) is visible in the step text; on Windows a freshly installed interpreter is not on the running launcher's PATH anyway.

D-018docs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

The lane resumed past D-016's round bound on the owner's direction in an attended coordinator session (2026-10-09): 'Can you bring WI-834 to completion so that it is able to land? I think the rounds can continue to run given the scope of this WI to try and clear the found issues.' Round 4 answers 012 F1 (D-017); the cycle continues with a narrow Sol round, the checkpoint (Terra reconciles 013-SPINE-CHANGES-r4.md; one combined sitting) and a fresh full-lane gate, repeating while full-lane rounds find valid defects. The coordinator also widened the builder's first answer: the launcher's candidates were narrower than its dev-setup's own runtime search, so a standalone check could report a runtime that run would not resolve (verified on this workstation: C:/Python38 first on PATH, 3.11 reachable only as py -3.11); the parity pin closes it.

D-019docs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

Owner ruling in the attended session (2026-10-09) on round 016 F2 (the guard hooks run as bare python, so an older interpreter first on PATH crashes the PreToolUse hook on tomllib and the call proceeds): bind at opt-in, machine-local. The hook opt-in writes the guard's hook groups with the absolute path of the floor-resolved interpreter it runs on into .claude/settings.local.json, never the committed .claude/settings.json; the relaunch launchers and the guard's injected command use the resolved interpreter too. This revises D-001's target file: D-019 supersedes D-001's .claude/settings.json as the opt-in's target (D-001's text stands as written; its other choices, which guard groups ship and that only they are merged, are unchanged). D-020docs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

Round 016 F1 (a PowerShell assignment such as $response = claude -p x hides its command word from the blackout hook; the hook's shell-reading class past its third round) went to dispute sitting 017 with the builder's FIX position; docs/reviews/wi-834/017-ADJUDICATE-1003705.md ruled R16F1 FIX: ordinary output capture inside the declared any-command-word coverage, fixed at the one shell-reading boundary with quoted right-hand values kept as data.

D-021docs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

Building round 5 (D-019, D-020): (1) the shell reader's words are a str subclass, kitlib.shell_line.Word, carrying quoted_at (the offset where its first quoted piece starts), so the guard tells PowerShell's $r = 'claude' (a value) from $r = claude (a command) without a second reading; coordinator_guard._assigned skips a leading assignment's targets and operator, also when the operator is written against the target ($r=claude), and a right-hand side opening with a quoted string or a variable is no command. (2) The opt-in binds each guard hook by replacing the example command's leading interpreter word with the opt-in's own sys.executable, as a forward-slash path in double quotes (read alike by the POSIX shell and cmd that Claude Code runs a hook command through); a re-run replaces the guard's own groups in .claude/settings.local.json and keeps every other group, so a different interpreter rebinds rather than duplicates. (3) GUARD is built at import from sys.executable, the hook's own interpreter. (4) The relaunch launchers are this repository's own, so their candidates are root run.cmd's / run.sh's (scripts/dev-setup.ps1's and scripts/dev-setup.sh's runtime search after .venv), pinned by the same parity test.

Alternative passed over

Mark quotedness with a separate segments() return shape; append rather than replace guard groups on re-enable; pass the interpreter to the relaunch launchers from launch_command.

Reversal cost

Low: each is local to its function and pinned by its test.

Why not escalated

Construction inside D-019's and D-020's rulings; a Word subclass keeps every existing segments() caller unchanged, and the relaunch probe is the one the run launchers already use (D-019 names it).

D-022docs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

Answering narrow round 018 within D-019 and D-020: (1) a PowerShell assignment's right-hand side that opens with a variable is data unless it is itself an assignment, so a chained $a = $b = claude -p x (which runs claude) is read through the same operator rule; (2) hooks_state reads the opt-in's command-level ownership by asking whether switching on would change the machine-local hooks at all (_merged(live, wanted) == live), so it and enable_hooks share one merge and cannot disagree.

Alternative passed over

Treat every variable right-hand side as data (missing the chained form); keep hooks_state's own group-membership test.

Reversal cost

Low: one branch in _right_hand and one line in hooks_state, each pinned.

Why not escalated

D-023docs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

Answering round 020's observations O1 and O2: (1) kitlib.shell_line.Word now carries the spans of every quoted piece (quoted_at is deleted, one representation), and the guard finds the first assignment operator none of whose characters was quoted; (2) the guard's own hook commands are defined once from the shipped example's own commands, as (interpreter word, rest) shapes, owned with the example's interpreter word or a double-quoted absolute path; (3) that ownership and the opt-in's merge moved out of coordinator_guard.py into a new pure module, kitlib/guard_hooks.py (guard_groups, bind, command_shapes, merged), because the round took coordinator_guard.py past the 1000-line module ratchet (1003 lines), whose rule is to decompose rather than bump; coordinator_guard.py keeps the file reading and writing (hooks_state, enable_hooks) and IF-280. D-024docs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

Round 024 F1 (PowerShell dot invocation, . claude -p x and $r = . claude -p x, read with . as the command word; the hook's shell-reading class in another round) went to dispute sitting 025 with the builder's FIX position, which asked for the coverage to be ruled a closed line. docs/reviews/wi-834/025-ADJUDICATE-22cf09c.md ruled R24F1 FIX and drew the line: the hook covers the word the shell's own grammar makes the command, so invocation operators (&, .) are inside the coverage, while commands that take a command as an argument (Start-Process, iex, cmd /c, sh -c, exec, command, builtin, nohup, xargs, script files) are outside it as the approved text says; findings against wrapper forms are dismissed by that line rather than reopened round by round, and widening it is an owner-level change to the coverage.

D-025docs/decisions/wi-834.toml

Decided

Round 028's one finding (Bash time -p claude -p x: the reader skips the time keyword but takes its -p option as the command) is answered with code under dispute sitting 025's ruled line, with no new sitting: time and its options are shell grammar, so the timed command is the command word, inside the coverage the ruling drew. To stop the class reopening one form per round, the build round derives the full set of grammar that can precede a command word in each dialect (the Bash reserved words and their options, the PowerShell invocation and assignment operators) from the shells' own grammar, and pins each, rather than fixing time -p alone.

D-011docs/decisions/wi-835.toml

Decided

The entry point refuses, with exit 2 and before anything launches or is written, a root that is not a lane: it must be the top of a linked worktree (git's worktree records through agent_common.worktree_records, whose first record is the primary checkout) on a branch whose committed tree still holds a claim under docs/work/active/<branch>/ (integrate.claimed_ids_on_branch, the integrator's own claim reader). A primary checkout, a detached HEAD, a branch with no claim and a directory outside any repository are each refused, naming why.

Alternative passed over

Refuse only the primary checkout (any linked worktree on any branch passes); or record the session log on trunk through a serialized, permitted trunk path.

Reversal cost

One function (lane_refusal) and its call in the entry point's input check.

Why not escalated

The owner's direction (D-008, confirmed) is that the entry point runs from the lane, and Sol's review showed a primary-checkout run commits its telemetry onto trunk, which integrate.audit rejects. A lane is defined by its claim, so the check reads the claim rather than trusting any branch name; both readers already exist, so no second primitive is written. integrate.py and this module share CMP-008, so the import adds no cross-component seam.

D-012docs/decisions/wi-835.toml

Decided

The entry point owns the verdict path the caller names exclusively: as its last check before launch it creates the path empty with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, so a path that exists, or that another call has already reserved, is refused (exit 2, 'name a fresh one'), and of two calls naming one absent path only the first launches. After the call, a non-zero exit or a timeout returns 1 without reading the file, and a reservation still empty (nothing written into it by this call's session) is a missing verdict (exit 1). A call refused before its launch (the sign-in refusal) removes its own still-empty reservation; a call that launched leaves the file, written or empty, for the coordinator to inspect.

Alternative passed over

Check only that the path does not exist (round 2, racy: a second call could write the verdict the first then reads); delete the reservation after every call; or write to an entry-point-chosen fresh path and report it.

Reversal cost

One function (reserve_verdict), one release on the pre-launch refusal, and one empty-file check in the report.

Why not escalated

Sol's round-2 review reproduced the race and the coordinator directed exclusive ownership rather than another existence check, keeping the path the caller names (the brief already embeds it, so the entry point cannot relocate the verdict without recomposing the brief). Leaving a launched call's file keeps the evidence of what that session did or did not write; a pre-launch refusal launched nothing, so its empty reservation carries no evidence and is removed so a retry may name the same path.

D-013docs/decisions/wi-835.toml

Decided

The sign-in probe reads only the documented answers: claude auth status is signed in only at exit 0 with output that is exactly one JSON object whose loggedIn is the boolean true, and missing only at exit 1 with loggedIn false; codex login status is read as a whole response: signed in only when, besides blank lines and codex's own PATH-alias warning (which 0.160.1 prints only for a home under the system temporary directory; a home under out/ gets none, probed), it is exactly one Logged in using <method> line at exit 0, and missing only when it is exactly Not logged in at exit 1. Everything else is unknown, which refuses, including a claude answer followed by any other text (a stderr warning included), a loggedIn of 1, and a codex answer beside a second answer or a fatal line (Sol round 2).

Alternative passed over

Extract the JSON object from surrounding text (round 1), or ignore the exit code for claude.

Reversal cost

Two small readers and a table in session_service.

Why not escalated

Sol's review showed the round-1 readers authorised undocumented answers; the coordinator directed the documented combinations only. A stray warning reading unknown refuses a launch that might have been fine, which is the safe direction under the no-fallback rule; the probe against this machine's signed-in ANTHROPIC home still reads signed-in.

D-014docs/decisions/wi-835.toml

Decided

AdjudicationRequest no longer carries template_paths/template_texts: it carries the operator's prompt_templates overrides (None on the coordinator route), so neither caller composes the identity and a new caller cannot compose a per-class one.

Alternative passed over

Keep the request's template fields and have each caller pass the retained set to governing_template (two callers reading the dial); or fold the retained set into session_keep.governing_hash, which would need session_keep to import adjudicate_brief, an import cycle (adjudicate_brief reaches session_keep).

Reversal cost

One request field, the identity line in adjudication_keep, and the reshaped governing_templates; the two callers each lose a line.

Why not escalated

D-015docs/decisions/wi-835.toml

Decided

reserve_verdict creates the verdict path's missing parent directories before its exclusive create. A parent that cannot be created (a path component that is a file, or a permission failure) is still refused with exit 2 as cannot be reserved, and an existing or concurrently reserved path still refuses as before. A call refused before launch removes its empty reservation but leaves any directories it created.

D-001docs/decisions/wi-838.toml

Decided

The lease-only record is the record with only family, route_id and lease keys (session_keep.is_lease_only): no session_id, no state, no generation. A record counts as live, a session to resume, only when its state is active or draining, so a lease-only record, or a bare one with its lease stripped, mints. The readers were fixed (_hold's live test, load_honoured's tombstone step), not the writer.

Alternative passed over

Write a full placeholder record at the mint (state retired or a new minting state, an empty session_id, generation 0), so every reader keeps seeing every key.

Reversal cost

One predicate and the shape written in session_keep._hold; no stored record outlives a call, so no migration.

Why not escalated

The build prompt orders a lease-only record and readers fixed rather than the writer special-cased. A placeholder state would also show a session-less record as retired or as a new state in the record's state vocabulary (IF-247), which every state reader would have to learn.

D-003docs/decisions/wi-838.toml

A crashed first call whose lease expires is retired like any unreleased lease and stays as a retired record with no session id.

Retire the abandoned lease-only record too, so both endings leave the same retired record.

One branch in session_keep._apply_tombstone.

The Done-when says keep_abandon removes the record and that a crashed first call's lease is retired as an unreleased lease is today; this follows both as written.

D-005docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

The combined class is named combined. Its row's Adjudicates cell holds <kind>:<id> tokens (kinds amendment, first-approval, done-when); each section is composed by compose itself for the row scoped to that kind's ids, with the section's verdict path written as the ## <kind> section of <file>, in the fixed order amendment, first-approval, done-when; any section that cannot compose refuses the sitting. Its verdict is one file with one ## <kind> heading per kind, each carrying its own kind's machine line, closed by SITTING: JUDGED kinds=<kinds>; the parser checks the headings match the named kinds and each section passes its own grammar. The Done-when grammar uses its own keyword DONE-WHEN: so its line is found inside a combined file.

Alternative passed over

A combined template that restates each kind's questions (a fork), or per-kind scope cells.

Reversal cost

The combined template, combined_values / _sitting_scopes / _sitting_refusal, and two table rows.

Why not escalated

The build prompt asks for a composition of the existing composers and parsers, not a fork; the token form keeps the scope a typed cell rather than prose.

D-010docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 2 (Sol MAJOR 2, 3, 5): a combined sitting's grammar has one home, a new shipped module kitlib/sitting.py (SITTING, KINDS, scopes for the <kind>:<id> tokens, sections for the ## <kind> verdict headings, own_section, and brief_scope, the one reader both act scopes in acceptance_record go through). adjudicate_brief, acceptance_record and intake all import it; acceptance_record.first_approval_scope and amendment_scope now read a combined row's tokens for their own kind, so each section's act is scoped as a single-kind row's would be.

D-011docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 2 (Sol MAJOR 5): a combined verdict is judged against the kinds its sitting REQUESTED, passed as verdict_refusal(..., kinds=...); with none given it is refused. The coordinator entry point reads the requested kinds off the composed brief's one SITTING: line (adjudicate_brief.requested_kinds). The loop passes none, so a combined verdict on the loop route is refused as owed; the loop never draws a combined sitting (no merge mints one). AMENDED round 17 (Sol final8 MAJOR 1): the loop route no longer passes none - it binds the composed request beside the verdict at composition (adjudicate_brief.bind_pending, the writer the entry point uses at reservation) and records the call against those bound kinds (bound_kinds), so a combined sitting the loop draws is judged against what it requested, on the same terms as the coordinator's.

Alternative passed over

Reversal cost

One keyword argument and one reader of the brief text.

D-012docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

D-013docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

D-014docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 3 (Sol r2 MAJOR 1): an adjudication's approval act may copy a registry in which it flipped a row OR re-attested one. merge_approval_refusal hands adjudication_approval_refusal the registries holding the rows the merge's act-ledger entries re-attested (_reattested_registries, read after reattest_scope_refusal has judged those rows against the amendment scope), and only a copy outside both is WIDENED. This also covers two single-kind rows (an amendment row and a first-approval row) acting in different registries, which had the same defect.

Reversal cost

Why not escalated

D-015docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 4 (the adjudicator's LLR-307 return): kitlib.done_when.claim_copy tells the claim copy apart from its two absences. ABSENT (the revision reads and holds no spec of the row under docs/work/active/<branch>/) is a row never claimed through that lane - a hand-cut lane, or an attended run on a row it did not claim - and stays RELEASED: there is no claimed Done-when, so nothing to bless; the merge-time mint keeps its stderr line saying the check did not run. UNREADABLE (no revision given, the revision cannot be read, or the listed copy cannot be) HOLDS at every hold point (build dispatch, hand close, merge ladder), each naming why through kitlib.done_when.unreadable_reason, and REFUSES the merge-time mint. The done-when brief refuses both, naming which. tests/test_module_size_ratchet.py takes a reviewed +2 for intake.py.

Alternative passed over

Hold on an absent claim too (every unclaimed or hand-cut run would then hold for a blessing no adjudication can give, since there is no claimed text to judge), or keep reading both as 'owes nothing' (an unreadable claim then fails open at every hold point).

Reversal cost

One reader (claim_copy) and its three callers (lane_hold, intake._done_when_drafts, adjudicate_brief._claim_at).

Why not escalated

The coordinator, relaying the adjudicator's return, directed holding the unreadable case and naming the legitimate absent one; the absent case is the one intake already reported as 'the check did not run' (a hand-cut lane, never claimed on trunk).

D-016docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 5 (Sol r3 MAJOR): carrier resolution has one home, acceptance_record._carrier_rows_at, returning the carrier file a side actually reads with its rows; _spine_rows_at is its rows, and _reattested_registries names each re-attested row's registry by that carrier (a legacy system-requirements.csv, not the canonical .toml path), so the copy a re-attestation writes is the one it is authorized for. To keep acceptance_record.py under the 1,000-line ratchet threshold (it reached 1,002), the amendment verdict's row reader (verdict_rulings and its tag table) moved to kitlib.verdict; acceptance_record keeps verdict_rulings as an alias for its callers and the LLR-278 cell.

Alternative passed over

Map the re-attested registry onto the flip side's touched-carrier rule (it reads staged names, which a re-attestation does not change), or bump the ratchet.

Reversal cost

Inline one resolver back into _spine_rows_at, and move one 20-line reader back.

Why not escalated

The coordinator directed one resolver resolving the carrier as the reader does, and decomposition into kitlib rather than a bump; the flip side already reports the carrier that changed, which for a flip is the same file this resolver reads.

D-017docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 6 (Sol r4 MAJOR): a tier's carrier set and its text reader now have one home, spine_carrier: tier_carriers(rel, id_col) picks the need carriers (.toml, legacy .md) for the needs file's tiers and the row carriers (.toml, legacy .csv) for every other, and tier_rows_from_text reads any of them (load_need_tier's markdown branch now shares _markdown_need_rows). acceptance_record lists no carrier itself: _carrier_rows_at, the two-tree walk's touched set and the squash check read every approval-act tier through those two. A combined act re-attesting a need on the markdown carrier is authorized for the .md copy it writes. tests/test_intake.py's write_sn moved from stakeholder-needs.csv, a carrier the need tier does not have, to .toml.

Alternative passed over

Add .md to acceptance_record's own carrier list (the third per-format patch), or resolve through spine_carrier.resolve, which reads the working tree, not a revision.

Reversal cost

Two functions in spine_carrier and four call sites in acceptance_record.

Why not escalated

The coordinator directed fixing the class through the kit's one carrier-aware reader; spine_carrier is that reader, and it gains a text-level entry because acceptance_record reads only revisions (its pinned import surface forbids the working tree).

D-018docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 7 (Sol r5 MAJOR): a first-approval act's snapshot copies are authorized by REGISTRY IDENTITY: acceptance_record._registry_identity maps any carrier path to its approval-act tier's canonical path through spine_carrier.tier_carriers, and adjudication_approval_refusal compares identities on both sides (WIDENED and WITHOUT ITS ANCHOR), so every carrier path of an authorized registry is its own act, the obsolete carrier's deleted copy included; a registry the act neither flipped nor re-attested in is still WIDENED on any of its paths. _reattested_registries now returns identities, and _carrier_rows_at folded back into _spine_rows_at (the carrier path is no longer needed). The gap is PRE-EXISTING: trunk 0ce475f7 refuses the same conversion under a plain approval flip of the needs file (WIDENED to stakeholder-needs.md).

Alternative passed over

Drop deleted copies from the inspected delta (a deleted copy of an unauthorized registry would then pass), or authorize the act's written carrier only.

Reversal cost

One identity function and four comparisons.

Why not escalated

The coordinator directed authorization by registry identity through the one resolver, keeping the unauthorized-copy guard; acceptance_record.py stays under the 1,000-line threshold (999 counted lines).

D-019docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 7 addendum (adjudication 005, LLR-307): both sides of a Done-when comparison are read in one shape, kitlib.done_when._copy_at: found (path, text, None); ABSENT (None, None, None) when the revision reads and holds no copy; UNREADABLE (None, None, why) when the listing or the copy cannot be read, never read as absent. claim_copy and spec_at both delegate to it. The one legitimate ABSENT case is the claim's (a row never claimed through this lane), which releases. A claimed row whose current copy is unreadable, or which has NO current copy in the lane (neither under active/<branch>/ nor in a closed folder: its claimed Done-when is gone, which no close accounts for), holds, naming why. A lane that deletes its Done-when section owes a blessing (every claimed item reads as changed). docs/stack.ini's smoke membership budget is re-stamped 2320 -> 2420, because tests/test_done_when_blessing.py (48 git-repo cases) stays in the smoke tier: approved TC-326 cites it at Smoke, so re-tiering it would make that row untrue.

Alternative passed over

Treat a missing current copy as an empty Done-when (a blessable digest of nothing), or re-tier the test module to the slow tier.

Reversal cost

One reader shape and one hold helper; one stamp.

Why not escalated

The coordinator relayed the adjudicator's finding and directed one shape for both sides; a lane losing its spec without a close is refused at merge anyway (it lands in no state folder), so holding it earlier names the cause sooner.

D-020docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 9 (Sol final gate, two MAJORs): a combined sitting's verdict grammar and its ONE validator live in kitlib.sitting (GRAMMAR, line_refusal, named_kinds, sitting_refusal, kind_part); adjudicate_brief's VERDICT_GRAMMAR entries for the sitting's kinds and its verdict check delegate there, and kitlib.done_when accepts a DONE-WHEN line only from a file kind_part finds valid (a single-kind Done-when verdict, or a combined sitting that passes the validator against the kinds it names, its line read from its own ## done-when section). A section heading is any kind-form ## <lower-case-token>, so an unrequested section refuses the sitting. Consequence: a sitting whose done-when section is missing, repeated, or whose DONE-WHEN line sits under another heading is now INVALID and covers nothing, so the merge's safety net mints the goalposts row rather than refusing the mint as ambiguous; only repeated Dispositions inside a valid done-when section still refuse.

Alternative passed over

Validate the sitting only at the coordinator's entry point (a rejected sitting's line then still blessed at the holds), or keep refusing the mint for those three shapes by reading invalid files.

Reversal cost

One validator module section and two delegations; the reader in done_when.

Why not escalated

SR-232 requires an invalid section to refuse the whole sitting with no other kind acting, and requires extra sections to refuse; reading an invalid file to refuse rather than mint would be a second path through a rejected verdict. Recorded because approved LLR-262's ambiguous-part clause narrows (listed for Terra).

D-021docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 10 (Sol final2, one class - parse, don't validate): kitlib.sitting.parse(text, brief, kinds) is the ONE parser of a verdict file into {kind: (label, fields)}: a single-kind verdict has no kind-form section and exactly one complete machine line; a combined sitting names exactly the requested kinds in its one SITTING line, holds exactly one section per requested kind and none other, and each section holds exactly one complete own-kind line and no other kind's line. adjudicate_brief.verdict_refusal (for the sitting's kinds and the sitting) and kitlib.done_when._verdicts both consume it; the Done-when line is the parse's. The requested kinds are BOUND in a separate file beside the verdict, <verdict>.requested (brief = <class>, kinds = <a;b>), which coordinator_adjudicate creates exclusively at reservation (after reserve_verdict, before launch; a pre-launch refusal removes both) and commits after the call in its own telemetry commit. The covering reader parses each verdict against its binding; with none, a file with no kind-form section is a single-kind Done-when verdict and a combined one covers nothing.

Alternative passed over

Write the requested kinds INTO the reserved verdict file (lost when the adjudicator rewrites the file), encode them in the verdict's file name, or read them from the composed brief recorded in the session log (not in the tree the holds read).

Reversal cost

One parser module section, the binding file and its two writers (reserve, commit).

Why not escalated

The coordinator directed one parser for both consumers and a binding that survives the adjudicator rewriting the verdict; a separate file does, and failing closed (unbound combined covers nothing) keeps a missing binding from releasing a hold. Recorded high-risk-adjacent: the binding is trusted as written, like the verdict beside it.

D-022docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 11 (Sol final3, three MAJORs of one class): acceptance is a RECORDED fact. The verdict's binding (<verdict>.requested) records outcome = pending|accepted|failed; kitlib.sitting.write_binding is its one writer (exclusive at reservation, pending) and adjudicate_brief.record_outcome is the one place a route records accepted (its own validation passed) or failed (a failed, timed-out or refused call, or an invalid verdict) and commits the binding. Both routes call it: coordinator_adjudicate after the call (from _report's result), and the loop's adjudication_bookkeeping after verdict_refusal. Every consumer reads verdicts through one reader, kitlib.sitting.accepted / accepted_at, which returns a parsed verdict only for an accepted, bound, valid file and None otherwise, never raising for a brief class it does not cover: the Done-when covering reader (and so dispatch, hand close, merge and the merge-time mint) and acceptance_record's held-rung re-attestation rung. LEGACY (no binding): a Done-when verdict covers nothing - DONE-WHEN verdicts are new in WI-841 and this lane's own Done-when is unchanged, so no legacy blessing exists to keep; a held-rung re-attestation naming an unbound verdict is refused at merge. Existing approvals stay readable: the rung judges only act-ledger entries a merge ADDS, so acts already on trunk (including those naming this lane's unbound verdicts 001-010) are never re-read; an in-flight act in an adopter repo naming a pre-upgrade unbound amendment verdict must be re-sat through a recording route (RESYNC says so).

Alternative passed over

Accept an unbound single-kind verdict as legacy when its text parses (keeps in-flight adopter acts mergeable, but reintroduces acceptance by inference), or record acceptance only on the coordinator route.

Reversal cost

The outcome field, one writer, one reader and four call sites.

Why not escalated

The coordinator directed acceptance as a recorded fact written only by the route that ran the call, one reader for every consumer, and a stated legacy rule; failing closed on unbound verdicts follows the owner's no-fallback rule. Recorded because it can refuse an in-flight adopter act at upgrade.

D-023docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 12 (Sol final4) widens D-022's reach in two ways. (1) ONE acceptance rule for both routes: adjudicate_brief.record_outcome takes the CALL's success as an input (coordinator: exit 0 and not timed out; loop: exit 0 and classify_outcome neither ERROR nor TIMEOUT) and judges the verdict itself (verdict_refusal against the bound kinds), recording accepted only when both hold - so neither route can record a failed call's verdict accepted. (2) At merge, EVERY act the merge adds that names a verdict - a re-attestation on a held or a released rung, and so any first approval taken in the same act (the snapshot tool lets an act name a verdict only beside a re-attestation) - must name a verdict kitlib.sitting.accepted_at reads as accepted (kitlib.sitting.unaccepted_refusal, after the held-rung rung so its specific refusals read first). D-022's legacy rule therefore now applies to released-tier acts too: an added act naming an unbound verdict is refused. Acts already on trunk stay readable - only ledger entries a merge adds are judged (acceptance_record._added_acts, now also behind reattested_between) - and an act naming no verdict is judged by the existing rules alone.

Alternative passed over

Check acceptance only on held rungs (Sol's bypass), or require every adjudication act to name a verdict (would refuse released-tier acts that legitimately name none today).

Reversal cost

One argument on record_outcome and its two callers; one kitlib refusal and its rung.

Why not escalated

The coordinator directed one rule for both routes and acceptance for every act naming a verdict, with D-022's legacy rule applied to acts merging from now on and existing acts readable; acceptance_record.py stays under the threshold (993 counted lines) by consolidating its added-act readers.

D-024docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 13 (Sol final5): a call's success has ONE derivation both routes share, session_service.call_succeeded(outcome): exit 0, no timeout, and no error result the CLI reported (is_error in its JSON result) - the real failure signals, never the displayed outcome (classify_outcome's COMMITTED can mask an error behind a commit) nor a commit's presence. Both routes hold the same session_service.Outcome: the coordinator passes its call's result; the loop's run_iteration records it on the session's plan (plan['call_ok']) for adjudication_bookkeeping, keeping session_bookkeeping's signature. The coordinator's _report uses the same test, so its narration matches what it records. record_outcome judges the verdict only when the call succeeded (call_ok and verdict_refusal(...)), so a failed call is recorded failed without its verdict being read (LLR-306's narration). A reservation refused because a binding already existed removes only this call's empty reservation (_release(path, bound=False)), never a binding another call owns.

Alternative passed over

Derive success separately in each route from code/timeout (Sol's bypass via is_error), or pass call_ok as a new session_bookkeeping argument (grows agent_loop past its ratchet for no gain).

Reversal cost

One function in session_service and its two callers; one plan key; one release flag.

Why not escalated

The coordinator directed one derivation from the real failure signals shared by both routes, ownership-aware cleanup, and a failed call recorded without reading its verdict; each is the smallest change that makes the stated rule true.

D-025docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 14 (Sol final6 MAJOR): close the unnamed path by DERIVING each act's authority, not by requiring --verdict. At merge, every act an adjudication lane adds is tied to its adjudication's ACCEPTED verdict whether or not it names one: each kind the added acts take (a flip needs first-approval, a re-attestation amendment) must be covered by a verdict kitlib.sitting.accepted_at reads as accepted among the bindings the branch itself changed under docs/reviews (kitlib.sitting.branch_verdicts), a combined sitting covering each kind it requested (kitlib.sitting.uncovered_refusal, after the named-verdict check). A lane whose only verdict for a kind is failed, pending, invalid or unbound has no authority for that kind's act. A named verdict must still itself be accepted (D-023). Legacy: an adjudication lane carrying no binding (a pre-upgrade in-flight lane) is refused at merge and re-sat through a recording route, extending D-022's legacy rule to every adjudication act; acts already on trunk are never re-read.

Alternative passed over

Refuse any adjudication act that omits --verdict (the snapshot tool forbids --verdict without --reattests, so every first-approval-only act would need that tool, the act command in three brief templates and the composed act slot changed, an adopter-facing CLI change), or read the verdict path off the claimed row (the row carries none; the loop and the coordinator each choose it per call).

Reversal cost

One kitlib refusal and its rung; the test fixtures' branch bindings.

Why not escalated

The coordinator asked for the rule that leaves no unnamed path; deriving from the lane's own recorded bindings covers named and unnamed acts alike with no change to the act CLI or the templates, and the bindings are what both routes already commit in the lane.

D-026docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 15 (Sol final7 MAJOR 2): adjudicate_brief.record_outcome now RETURNS its decision, (outcome, why), and the loop's adjudication_bookkeeping sets its completion obligation (adjudication_owed) from that same decision rather than a second verdict check: a failed call (call_ok false) keeps its obligation, is recorded failed, and its verdict is never read, so the worker cannot finish DONE and the re-sit is not lost. A missing root or verdict path is owed without recording. Sol final7 MAJOR 1 (row-tied coverage) was NOT built: by the coordinators' standing rule a further crafted-input finding goes to the independent adjudicator as a named dispute, whose ruling sets the fix or files it as a follow-up.

Alternative passed over

Keep two decisions (record from call success and validation; clear the obligation from validation alone), which let a failed call finish DONE.

Reversal cost

One return value and the bookkeeping that consumes it.

Why not escalated

The coordinator directed one decision consumed in both places; the row-tied coverage change was explicitly withdrawn from this round.

D-027docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 16 (owner ruling: an act's authority comes from the judgement of ITS rows; Sol final7 MAJOR 1). SUPERSEDES D-025's kind-only coverage. At merge, every ROW an added adjudication act flips must be ruled APPROVE in a first-approval part, and every row it re-attests ruled MEANING or CLARITY in an amendment part, of an ACCEPTED verdict among the bindings the branch carries (single-kind or combined; kitlib.sitting.uncovered_refusal over judged_rows), whether or not the act names a verdict; an accepted verdict over other rows authorizes nothing, and each unjudged row is named with its kind. A NAMED --verdict must be accepted AND judge each row the act re-attests (kitlib.sitting.unaccepted_refusal / _named_line). The held-rung CLARITY-only rule stays acceptance_record's, now reading the accepted part's parsed rows. The per-row rulings come from the ONE row reader, kitlib.verdict.row_rulings (generalised from verdict_rulings to each sitting kind's tags and fail-toward rule: MEANING over CLARITY, RETURN over APPROVE), exposed by kitlib.sitting.accepted as each part's fourth element; no second row parser. D-022's legacy rule and D-025's upgrade effect stand (an adjudication lane with no accepted, row-judging binding is refused at merge).

Alternative passed over

Keep kind coverage (an accepted sitting over other rows authorizes this act - Sol's bypass), or require every act to name a verdict (the act CLI forbids --verdict without --reattests).

Reversal cost

The row-coverage refusal, the named-verdict row check and the generalised row reader; the fixtures' judged rows.

Why not escalated

The owner ruled the scope; the coordinator directed row coverage through the existing parse with no second row parser, and the D-025 supersession recorded here.

D-028docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 18 (Sol final9 MAJOR): the Done-when hold moves to the ONE point a session is actually selected for dispatch. run_iteration now calls agent_loop.routed_session, which runs route_session and then, for a routed session that builds (neither a review, a critique nor an adjudication brief - the worker assignment, a build or a rework), asks build_hold and exits with its banner before anything launches. worker_endstate holds nothing of its own any more (its building arm is restored to its pre-WI-841 shape), so no early-return arm before routing (the dirty-tree deferral after a completed WI trailer, or a resumed lane's first iteration over a Blocked-WI trailer) can bypass the hold. route_session (complexity 37) and run_iteration (15) are not grown: the hold rides the routing call's existing int-return arm.

Alternative passed over

Keep the hold in worker_endstate and add it to each early-return arm (two hold sites, and any future arm would need it too), or put it inside route_session (complexity 37, over budget, and its hold banner names adjudication rows).

Reversal cost

One wrapper function and its call; worker_endstate's three restored lines.

Why not escalated

The coordinator directed one hold at the point a BUILD or rework is selected, after routing decides, removing the hold from worker_endstate if redundant; the wrapper is the smallest change that keeps run_iteration within budget.

D-029docs/decisions/wi-841.toml

Decided

Round 19 (Sol final10 MAJOR): the one parser reads machine lines strictly one PHYSICAL line at a time (kitlib.sitting._keyword_lines: a line whose first token is KEYWORD:, split into tokens; no regex spans a newline). Every such line counts, complete or not - a bare keyword, a label carried onto the next line, a label outside the enum or a missing field=value token makes the verdict invalid (_machine_lines / _machine_line / _incomplete). A single-kind verdict carries exactly one complete line of its kind and none of another sitting keyword; a combined sitting carries exactly one SITTING line and one complete line per requested kind across the WHOLE file (a keyword line outside every section included) and none of an unrequested kind (_keyword_count_refusal), checked after each section's own line so section-located messages stay. named_kinds and own_section use the same per-line reader. The MINOR: coordinator_adjudicate's Contract IF-285 (and IF-284) paragraphs now state the full success condition, session_service.call_succeeded.

Alternative passed over

Patch the regex so its whitespace class no longer spans a newline, and keep counting only matched lines (a bare keyword line would still go uncounted).

Reversal cost

Four small functions in kitlib.sitting replacing two regexes.

Why not escalated

The coordinator directed strict per-physical-line parsing in the one parser every reader uses, counting every keyword line complete or not.

D-001docs/decisions/wi-842.toml

Decided

The hand-back is gated by the dial like the hooks and the claim boundary: at [coordinator] context_guard_pct = 0 hand_back returns None (exit 0) before reading the handoff or the lease and writes nothing, so the session-protocol close-out can run it unconditionally.

Alternative passed over

Run it whatever the dial, as take, release, clear and request-relaunch do today (none of them checks the dial), freeing a lease that a dial-0 repo never uses.

Reversal cost

One guard line in hand_back and one test.

Why not escalated

The build prompt orders it ('Dial 0: every entry point returns before reading or writing') and the Done-when requires 'Dial 0 still writes nothing'. Noted as a finding: the existing take/release/clear/request-relaunch do not check the dial, so the module header's 'every entry point returns before reading or writing' is true of the hooks, the claim and now the hand-back, not of those four.

D-003docs/decisions/wi-842.toml

Decided

The hand-back's event is handback with fields session, handoff (the resolved path) and was_draining; the lease is replaced by the empty record, exactly as the owner's release leaves it, so a latched drain ends with it and the next take installs an unlatched holder.

Alternative passed over

Keep a tombstone in the lease (the last holder and its handoff), or unlatch while keeping the lease held until the next take.

Reversal cost

The event fields and one assertion; a tombstone would change what take and claim_refusal read as free.

Why not escalated

The Done-when says it 'frees the lease and records a handback event naming the handoff', and that the latch clears 'with the lease, as a successor's take does'; the empty record is the existing meaning of a free lease.

D-004docs/decisions/wi-842.toml

Decided

The holder and session-prompt checks request_relaunch already made are extracted into two shared helpers (_not_holder, _promptless) that request_relaunch and hand_back both call; request_relaunch's refusal texts are unchanged, and the hand-back's non-holder refusal appends the owner's release command.

Alternative passed over

Copy the two checks into hand_back.

Reversal cost

Inline two helpers.

Why not escalated

The build prompt orders reuse over duplication; behaviour of request_relaunch is unchanged and its tests pass.

D-005docs/decisions/wi-842.toml

Decided

The hand-back is tagged Implements: SR-229, LLR-300 (the lease row, whose module is coordinator_guard.py) and is to be listed in LLR-300's code_symbol; no new LLR is proposed, and the reserved LLR-311 is left unused.

A new LLR-311 for the hand-back, or tagging it to LLR-301 (the relaunch row that shares the handoff check).

Reversal cost

Re-tag one function and move one code_symbol entry.

The hand-back is a lease transfer, which LLR-300 owns alongside take, release and clear; SR-229 is the requirement the spec cites.

D-006docs/decisions/wi-842.toml

Decided

The skill's close-out names the hand-back as the end of every coordinator close-out, latched or not, that requests no relaunch, and the mirrors under .claude/skills and .agents/skills were refreshed by byte copy of the source, verified with gen_skills_index.py --check-agents, rather than by running bootstrap.py --sync against this repo.

Run bootstrap.py --dest . --sync, which also re-materializes every other per-agent skill subtree.

None: the result is byte-identical to what --sync writes for this skill.

D-003docs/decisions/wi-846.toml

Decided

Lock contention (Sol round 1, MAJOR 3): release-only paths (an authentication failure's lease release and the keep-warm skip) write a lockless release marker first, the tombstone protocol in a release-only mode, applied at once when the lock frees within a second, else by the next locked read before any expired-lease retirement. The same class on keep_bookkeep's ordinary path predates this row and is filed as WI-858 rather than built here.

Alternative passed over

Catch StoreBusy and retry; or widen this row to make keep_bookkeep durable too.

Reversal cost

The marker's release-only mode and its reader; WI-858 builds the ordinary path on it.

Why not escalated

A marker that never waits on the lock makes the contention failure unrepresentable for a release; a retry only narrows it. keep_bookkeep's fix carries the call's observation and reset decision, a wider store-protocol change than this row's surface, and the cycle stops a round on a consolidation outside the spec.

D-004docs/decisions/wi-846.toml

Decided

Sol round 2's MAJOR 1 (a JSON-escaped or line-split token slips past the exact-value redaction) is answered by a stated bound in the IF-282 contract, not a further redaction pass: the redaction removes verbatim occurrences; no standard encoder (Python json.dumps, Node JSON.stringify) escapes the token's ASCII characters, and a split needs the child to disclose a value it already holds, which D-002 records it can do anywhere.

Alternative passed over

Redact the decoded event before every decoded-consumer sink as well; or send the disagreement to the adjudicator as a named dispute before building.

Reversal cost

A decoded-sink redaction pass can be added later; it would not close base64, reversal or splitting either.

Why not escalated

The builder's evidence shows the forms are adversarial only, and the adversary is the process D-002 already cedes the token to; the contract then states exactly what the guard covers. If the fresh full-lane review re-raises the finding, it becomes a named dispute for the adjudicator.

D-005docs/decisions/wi-846.toml

Decided

D-003 is superseded by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-08, verbatim 'Move it to WI-858': WI-846 drops the lockless release marker (its release-only mode, the shared marker view and the clock-first ordering exist only for it) and releases an authentication failure's lease under the store lock, as before round 2; store-lock contention on every path is WI-858's. The three Codex Sol rounds' contention findings are WI-858's test list. Round 1 MAJOR 3: the store lock held across an authentication-failure call made StoreBusy escape and left the lease, and once it expired the next call retired the session 'lease expired unreleased' and minted afresh. Round 2 MAJOR 4: a release-only marker published under contention made due_routes skip the record, so keep-warm never applied it. Round 2 MAJOR 5: a locked reader that read the marker before a release was published retired the expired lease anyway. Round 3 MAJOR 2: a reader holding an older marker unlinked a newer release published while it held the lock, without applying it, and the current session was retired.

Alternative passed over

Keep the marker in WI-846 and give release markers distinct identities consumed by identity (another build and review round); or send the class to the adjudicator as a named dispute.

Reversal cost

The removed marker code is reachable in the lane's history (5493eccd, ea3fa3f7) and in archive/lanes once the lane lands.

Why not escalated

The owner ruled it directly when asked; this entry records what the coordinator did under that ruling and keeps the findings WI-858 must answer.

D-006docs/decisions/wi-846.toml

Decided

Codex Sol round 4's three MAJOR findings (the route snapshot split between selection, preparation, keep-warm and the version probe) were sent back to the builder as a precise design (prepare_launch takes the selected row and never rereads the registry), not to the adjudicator as a named dispute, although it is the third round on the launch-preparation class.

Alternative passed over

Name a dispute for an independent adjudicator, as the cycle asks at a third round of crafted-input findings.

Reversal cost

One more build round; if round 5 draws the class again, it goes to the adjudicator.

Why not escalated

Nothing is in dispute: builder and reviewer agree on the principle (one selected snapshot), and round 4 implemented round 3's direction the wrong way round to avoid touching agent_loop. The coordinator entry point also has no dispute brief class (a gap for the handoff). Recorded so the owner can overrule the deviation.

D-007docs/decisions/wi-846.toml

Decided

Codex Sol round 5's two MAJORs (the version probe resolving its executable from the ambient PATH, and the probe receiving and persisting the credential) were sent back to the builder as a precise construction (Prepared carries the one resolved executable; the probe runs with the credential withheld), not to an adjudicator, although D-006 said a repeat of the class would go to one.

Alternative passed over

Name a dispute for an independent adjudicator, as D-006 recorded.

Reversal cost

One adjudicator sitting and possibly one more build round.

Why not escalated

Nothing is in dispute: Sol named the exact invariant (one executable resolution shared by probe and launch) and the builder has not contested it; the coordinator entry point still has no dispute brief class. The second finding is a round-5 regression, not the class.

D-008docs/decisions/wi-846.toml

Decided

A retained launch whose runner does not resolve on the composed launch PATH is refused at preparation, before any lease or record, with the same SigninRefused the competing-credential and --bare refusals raise, naming the runner and whether the PATH searched is the route's declared one or the ambient one; Prepared.executable is then always an absolute path, and neither the probe nor the launch has an empty-executable branch. Tests prepare with do-nothing runners first on PATH (the shared retained_runners fixture), never by bypassing the resolution. Surfaced, not built: the family-level sign-in status probe (a status command such as codex login status) still resolves its runner over the ambient PATH; it takes no route row, and a follow-up could have require_signin take the Prepared launch.

Alternative passed over

Leave Prepared.executable empty for an unresolved runner: the probe runs nothing and the launch keeps the template's bare name (the round-6 first build), where Windows CreateProcess searches the parent's path.

Reversal cost

The refusal in _resolve_executable and the test fixture; the empty branch would return in the probe and the argv substitution.

Why not escalated

The owner's standing rule settles it: fix the single point of failure, never add a fallback or degenerate path. The bare-name launch was exactly the split Sol round 5's MAJOR 1 named, and test convenience is not a reason to keep it.

Every writer the kit ships (intake's mints, wi_convert) writes the list, and no spec in this repo carries another shape, so refusing a shape nobody writes costs no adopter work while each accepted spelling is a second reading two paths must keep equal. D-003docs/decisions/wi-881.toml

Decided

Answer sitting 001's second return by waiting, not softening: after the kill, _kill_tree returns only once the group (POSIX) or job (Windows, its active-process count) is empty, and raises if it is not empty within one stated bound of 10 s. SR-238's 'before the coordinator continues' then holds as written, the test asserts the grandchild is gone the moment run_session returns, with no grace period, and the stated bound is the overrun after which the coordinator stops with an error instead of continuing. Built (round 2): on Windows the job's active-process count reads zero a few milliseconds before a terminated process is signalled (the builder's measurement, 2026-10-10), so the wait also holds a SYNCHRONIZE handle on each job member taken just before the terminate and waits until each is signalled; the count alone left the interruption test red. Residual, recorded with D-002's: on POSIX a zombie still counts as a group member, so under a PID 1 that never reaps (a container run without an init) every deadline kill raises after the bound. That failure is loud, not silent; RESYNC_PACK tells adopters to run under a reaping init.

Alternative passed over

Keep the kill asynchronous and state a grace bound in SR-238 (for example, descendants end within 5 s of the coordinator continuing), asserting that bound in the test.

Reversal cost

Low: the wait is the tail of one function.

Why not escalated

The sitting offered both routes; waiting makes the stated threshold the code's behaviour rather than a tolerance.

D-005docs/decisions/wi-881.toml

D-006docs/decisions/wi-881.toml

Decided

Answering full-lane gate 006's F1, the spawn boundary owns the child (and its job) until it returns it, and one try/finally in run_session owns it from there, ending the tree on any exit but a natural one; the waiter's own interrupt handler is retired into that owner. Not built: an interruption that lands inside the standard library's process creation, before the child object reaches the kit's code (POSIX: during Popen's exec handshake, a running child is lost; Windows: at Popen's return, the child is left suspended and never runs). It is recorded as a residual in SR-238's Rationale.

Alternative passed over

Defer SIGINT around the launch (signal.pthread_sigmask on POSIX, a deferred handler on Windows), which works on the main thread only and adds signal plumbing to every launch.

Reversal cost

Low: a later row can add the deferral inside _spawn_session.

Why not escalated

The window is the stdlib's own, a few instructions wide, and on Windows the left-behind child never runs; recording it keeps SR-238 true without a main-thread-only mechanism.

D-007docs/decisions/wi-881.toml

Decided

Answering narrow review 007's F1, a failure to end the session's tree raises agent_session.TreeNotEnded, a BaseException no except OSError or except Exception catches, so run_session's launch-error conversion can no longer turn it into a session result. When the cleanup fails while an interrupt is in flight, TreeNotEnded wins (it names what the operator must act on) and the interrupt stays in its chain. One sibling site outside this row's surface is left for its own row: session_service.KeepWarm._ping swallows every exception on its background thread, so a keep-warm session whose tree could not be ended is recorded and dropped. Filed as a follow-up row on trunk at this session's close.

Alternative passed over

Subclass OSError and audit every handler, or widen this lane into session_service to carry the error from the keep-warm thread to the dispatcher.

Reversal cost

Low: one exception class; callers that need cleanup catch BaseException and re-raise, as RESYNC_PACK tells adopters.

Why not escalated

It makes the failure unrepresentable as a result at its one owner; the keep-warm site follows the stop-and-file rule for work outside the spec's surface.

D-006high riskdocs/decisions/coordinator-2026-10-14.toml

Decided

WI-911's round-2 scope critique (S2, MAJOR) is adopted: a review brief's convergence marking lets a non-convergence-class MAJOR pass to a successor row instead of holding the landing, so the row gains a Trust section. The marking is a construction, not a convention: only review_brief.py review renders it, from a new --stance choice (ordinary by default, or convergence) as one fixed ROUND FACTS line, refused on a narrow round; a hand-appended line is not a marking and the unattended loop marks none; the reviewer applies the reduced blocking rule only on that rendered line, and the coordinator lets a successor-marked finding leave the landing's path only for a round its lane decisions record shows as one of the three convergence rounds at the verdict's reviewed tip. Every failure leaves the stricter ordinary stance.

Alternative passed over

A coordinator-appended stance line named in the recipes, with the Trust section stating its failure rules (no code change); or reviewers that never relax, grading every round alike, with the coordinator alone applying the convergence blocking rule from the round's position.

Low before the claim: amend WI-911's deliverables 3 and 7 and its Trust section, and re-critique.

Why not escalated

The critique's remedy asked for a Trust section, which the coordinator writes before the claim (coordinator-cycle section 1); the rendered choice reuses review_brief.py's existing round model, which already refuses a narrow round's shape in a full one. The Trust ruling itself goes to the owner to confirm or overrule, as every row's does.
